name: evolution
description: "How Crustify repairs and improves itself from what its campaigns expose: goals, signals, proposals, lessons, evolution branches, validation, review, autonomy, adoption, the record of what landed and how evolution itself evolves. Read before filing a defect in Crustify or a tool, proposing or making a change to either, or recording a campaign's lesson."
---

# Evolution

How a campaign changes the harness that runs it, Crustify's skills, agents, templates and
providers, its tools and the tools it lacks, and how its agents propose changes to the
campaign's artifacts that other roles own. A campaign exposes what the harness gets
wrong, what it constrains needlessly and what it repeats by hand; evolution turns that
evidence into changes, under the autonomy the settings' `evolution` answer grants, and
this guidance itself among them. Where a change goes within Crustify is
[`authoring`](../authoring/SKILL.md)'s.

## 1. Goals

Every change is judged against Crustify's goals, [`GOALS.md`](../../../GOALS.md), read in
full before the first proposal: a change serves one of them, or it is not made. The goals
are evolved too, when the evidence questions them, as `GOALS.md` describes.

A change to a tool is judged against that tool's own goals and non-goals too, the document
its tool skill names, read in full before the first change to the tool: they keep what the
tool is from drifting, such as an analysis that stays syntactic and does no data-flow
analysis. A change that departs from one of them is proposed, not made, and says so. A
tool with no such document has every change that alters what it is, rather than fixing or
extending what it does, proposed, not made.
<!-- TODO: ffimap has no goals document yet. -->

## 2. Signals

Evolution starts from evidence a campaign produces, never from taste:

| signal | what it suggests |
|---|---|
| a tool that crashes, or reports what the source contradicts | a defect in the tool |
| skills that contradict each other, or an agent prompt that leads its agent wrong | a defect in the spec |
| a rule an agent works around, or that forces a worse result than its omission would | an overconstraining rule, loosened or removed |
| review findings that recur across batches, in one objective or category | a rule the how-to skills lack |
| failed or rerun batches, and plan corrections | a defect in planning, scheduling or packing |
| the user's corrections | a rule, or a lesson of the campaign |
| cost or time outliers, in the dashboard | waste in batch sizing, gates or tooling |
| one representation hand-written in several places, or a TODO met again and again | a primitive or tool feature that is missing |
| one procedure repeated by hand: the same script written again, the same queries run in sequence | a tool, or a subcommand of one |
| a signal evolution missed, or a proposal that proved wrong | a defect in this guidance |
| a goal no decision cites, two that keep conflicting the same way, or a well-founded change no goal serves | a change to the goals |

A proposal needs one of these, with its evidence: a defect, a failure, a recurring
finding, a workaround or a measured waste. Fewer, well-founded proposals serve better than
many small ones: a change made for style alone, or for completeness, or to have proposed
something, is not made.

## 3. Destinations

Each signal goes to one destination:

- **the campaign alone**: what a setting or a task message settles, which changes nothing
  of Crustify;
- **a lesson**: a rule that holds for this target alone, recorded in the campaign's
  [`LESSONS.md`](#5-lessons);
- **the spec**: a skill, an agent, a template or a provider, where `authoring` places it;
- **a tool**: its code, its documentation or its tests, or a new tool; or
- **a campaign artifact**: the plan, the dependencies, the schedule or the dashboard, where
  the evidence shows one wrong or improvable and another role owns it. Its owner applies
  the proposal or declines it, a plan's at the next planner run.

A rule an agent cannot follow because its host refuses it, a write or a tool call
blocked, or a launch mode that withholds what the role needs, is a defect of that host's
provider, not of the rule: the provider prevents it with whatever its host offers, its
agents' definitions, the settings and permissions it installs, its hooks, the mode it
launches runs in, or the host's memory, and the spec is not bent around one host. Until
the provider's change lands, a run that meets the refusal neither works around it nor drops
what it could not do: it hands that to the assistant, in its final message, and the
assistant carries it out.

The test between a lesson and the spec is generality: a rule that can only be stated in
the target's own names is a lesson, and one the spec takes is stated without them, as it
would hold for any C codebase.

## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as
its `PROPOSAL.md`: the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it
cites; its destination; the change, or the patch; how it was validated; its review's
verdict; and its status, `open`, `landed`, with the commit it landed as, or `declined`,
with why. A lesson is not
filed as a proposal: `LESSONS.md` records it.

A defect in a tool found while reviewing is such a proposal, not a finding on the reviewed
code, and is filed with its reproducer.

## 5. Lessons

The campaign's lessons sit in `crustify/LESSONS.md`, read by every run of the campaign
before its first step. Each is one rule, with the evidence it rests on and its scope, the
modules, items or stages it holds for. A lesson a second campaign records again is
generalized into the spec, by a proposal citing both.

## 6. Changes

A campaign evolves each component, Crustify or a tool, on a working branch of its own in
that component's repository, `<campaign-id>/devel`, the campaign id being the name of the
campaign's repository. It is forked from the component's `devel` when the campaign first
needs it, and the campaign's runs read and run the component from its checkout, so that a
campaign runs on what it has changed and no other campaign does.

A change is made on a branch named `<campaign-id>/evolution/<slug>`, forked from that
working branch, in a worktree beside the repository that lives only while the change is
made. A branch holds one concern. Once the change lands on the working branch, by a
fast-forward, the worktree is purged and the branch deleted. Its commits take the identity
[`versioning`](../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Identity section gives the
campaign's.

- A change to the spec follows `authoring`: written once, in the place its kind belongs,
  as generally as the evidence allows.
- A change to what a tool does comes with a regression test: the reproducer of a defect
  becomes one, and a new behaviour gets one that fails without it. A change to its
  documentation alone adds none, unless the defect it fixes has a reproducer, which becomes
  a test or a doctest. A packaging defect's reproducer becomes a test too, run
  against a build installed as a dependent installs it. The tool's whole suite passes, its
  opt-in tests included wherever the change touches what they cover.
- A new tool is drafted and tested where it serves a repeated procedure, preferably as a
  subcommand of an existing tool within that tool's goals, or as a script in the skill
  that describes its use, as `authoring` places one; a tool of its own repository is
  merged upstream only with the user's approval.

A fix that unblocks the campaign, or that would prevent a defect in later campaigns, is
landed on the working branch as soon as it is reviewed, rather than batched.

## 7. Validation

A tool's change is validated by its tests, the regression test it adds among them.

A spec change that a failure prompted is validated by running again what failed, the item,
the batch or the stage, under the change: a lightweight run, without the tests or gates
the failure does not need to show. The proposal records what the run produced before and
after, and a change whose rerun still fails does not land. A spec change no failure
prompted, such as a rule loosened or a waste removed, is validated the same way where its
effect is in doubt, on the item its evidence came from.

A rerun shows that a change answers the case that exposed it, not that it holds: that is
watched in the campaigns after it lands, as [Record](#11-record) describes.

## 8. Review

Every change is reviewed before it lands, on its evolution branch, by a run other than the
one that made it. The review reads the proposal, the change and its validation, and checks
that:

- the proposal's evidence shows the signal, and the change answers it;
- the change serves a goal, and a tool's stays within the tool's own goals;
- it is placed and written as [`authoring`](../authoring/SKILL.md) describes, and states
  no rule in the target's names;
- its validation was run, and shows what the proposal says;
- its entry of [Record](#11-record), which the change or its proposal drafts, names a
  recurrence signal a campaign would observe, and `test` only where its test checks all of
  it; and
- whether it weakens a check, which the verdict marks.

A review runs under the campaign's working branch of the component, never under the change
it reviews, and reads the change from its branch. Its task pins the commit it reviews, and
only that commit lands, by a fast-forward of the working branch: a commit added after the
verdict, or one a rebase or cherry-pick makes, is reviewed again. Its checks are this section's and its
role's; the task message of the run that asks for it adds to them, and never relaxes them.
A review reads as deeply as the change reaches: a change to documentation alone is read; a
tool's code, a check, a soundness fix and every rule of the spec are reviewed with their
validation run again.

The verdict is recorded in the proposal's Review section, approved or rejected, with its
reasons; a rejection leaves the proposal open for another change or for the user.

What only records what was decided, a status of [Record](#11-record) a check changes or a
proposal's status, verdict and review, changes no rule and is not reviewed; an entry is
reviewed with its change.

A change that weakens a check, a gate, a test, a lint, a review objective, a tool's
detection or a rule of this skill, is marked so in the verdict and in its entry of the
record, since a run that can loosen what judges it passes by loosening it: the user reads
each such change on its own before `devel` takes it, as [Autonomy](#9-autonomy) describes.

## 9. Autonomy

The settings' `evolution` answer sets how far a campaign evolves the harness:

| answer | what lands on the campaign's working branches |
|---|---|
| `off` | nothing: no proposal, no lesson |
| `propose` | nothing but the record's statuses: proposals and lessons are filed, and no rule changes |
| `repair` | each fix of a defect |
| `evolve` | also each improvement and discovery |

A change lands on its component's working branch as soon as its review approves it,
without the user's approval: the working branch is the campaign's own, and nothing else
runs on it. `GOALS.md` is the exception: a change to it is proposed, never made, since it
is what every other change is judged against.

A component's `devel` is the user's gate. It takes a campaign's working branch only with
the user's approval, asked for at each module's end and at the campaign's end, with the
record's entries since the last advance, those the review marked as weakening a check
first. Where `devel` has moved meanwhile, the working branch takes it by merge before it
is offered. What the user declines is reverted on the working branch or stays there, as
they say, and is recorded so; where it weakened a check, what landed under it is reviewed
again, by review batches with `revisit`, as [Adoption](#10-adoption) schedules them for a
soundness fix. Merging a component's `devel` into its `main`, and merging a
new tool upstream, need the user's approval too.

A run that a defect blocks does not work around it. Where the answer lets fixes land, it
makes the fix on its evolution branch; under `propose` it files the proposal, with its
reproducer, and the user is asked at once whether the fix is to be made; and it ends,
reporting which. The fix is reviewed and lands, and the run is run again, as a failed
batch is.

## 10. Adoption

Every run's `task.json` records the revisions of Crustify and the tools it launched
under, as [`task-schema`](../../artifacts/task-schema/SKILL.md)'s Run fields section
describes. A change that lands on a working branch takes effect as it lands: the runs launched
after it record its revision, and a run under way when it lands, which its recorded
revisions and its landing's date tell, may have followed either. What landed before it
under the old rules stays, unless the change fixes a soundness
defect: then the landings it affects are reviewed again, by a review batch with
`revisit`.

At each module's end, the campaign's evolution is consolidated: recurring lessons are
proposed for the spec, open proposals are landed as the autonomy allows, the working
branches are offered to the user for `devel`, the revisit batches a soundness fix or a declined weakening calls for are scheduled, and the watched changes
of the record are checked against the module, as an audit checks them at its end.

## 11. Record

Every change that lands is recorded in Crustify's own repository, in
[`EVOLUTION.md`](../../../EVOLUTION.md), whatever component it changed, so that a later
campaign can tell whether it held. An entry gives the campaign and proposal the change
came from, the component and commit it landed as, the signal it answered, its recurrence
signal and its status, with a change that weakens a check marked so in its status. A change
no proposal filed names its campaign and `no proposal` in its place, with where it came
from. The entry is drafted with its change, in the change itself for a
change to Crustify and in its proposal for a change to a tool, so that the review reads it,
and is committed on Crustify's working branch of the campaign as the change lands. The record holds every
change landed since it began, on 2026-11-12; what landed before is not recorded.

The recurrence signal is what a campaign would observe if the issue were back, in what a
campaign produces anyway: a review finding of a category, a run that fails for a cause, a
tool's error, a correction the user repeats. A change whose regression test checks all of
it has `test` in its place and is not watched. One with no signal a campaign could observe
has `none`, with why, and is not watched either.

A watched change is checked at each module's end, and at an audit's end, in every campaign,
against that module's or audit's findings, failed runs, proposals and corrections. It is:

- `watched` from its landing;
- `recurred` once its signal is met again, with the evidence, which opens a proposal that
  cites the entry: the change was wrong or partial, or the validation and review that
  passed it were; and
- `confirmed` once a campaign other than the one it came from has ended, having exercised
  it, without the signal.

The record is committed on Crustify's working branch of the campaign, each entry with its
change and each check at its module's end, and reaches `devel` with it. Rows are appended
in landing order and statuses edited in place, so that a merge of two campaigns' working
branches keeps both campaigns' rows, ordered by their landing.
Under `propose`, where no rule changes, the check still runs and its statuses are
committed all the same, since a record commit changes no rule, and they are put to the user
with the campaign's proposals. Under `off`, it does not run.

## 12. Evolving evolution

Evolution evolves from its own record, as everything else does from a campaign's. At a
campaign's end the record and the campaign's proposals are read for what repeats: changes
that recurred; changes the review rejected or the user declined, by cause; signals a run
met that no proposal answered; how long a blocking defect held its run; and what the
reviews bought for what they cost: per change, the findings each round made that held, those
its author's own validation had already caught, the rounds it took and their cost. How deep
a review reads, and how many rounds a kind of change gets, follow from that evidence, not
from a fixed rule. Each is a
signal of this guidance, as [Signals](#2-signals) lists them, and its proposal is on this
skill, on the agents' evolution rules or on what the review checks.

Such a proposal is validated and reviewed as any other, and is marked as one that changes
what checks the rest, so that the user reads it on its own before `devel` takes it, as
[Autonomy](#9-autonomy) describes.

content.content: --- name: ffimap description: "Deterministic counts and sites of a Rust crate's unsafe and FFI surface. Read before a batch lands (its safe-boundary scan and safety-audit cells), before planning an audit's worksets, and when reviewing for unsafety, contracts or UB." --- # ffimap ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them. It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document: ```bash ffimap > .json ``` Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`, `as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs `from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`: ```bash ffimap --ffibox --sys-crates --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \ --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \ > .json ``` In a port campaign, a scan names with `--features` the export feature of every module not yet switched, as the [conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Export features section names them, so that the `ffi_export` gateways compiled under them are counted. Every scan names the module's unsafe regions, as the conventions' Unsafe regions section names them, with `--regions`. Two scans are compared only when they name the same seams, regions and features. Its counters form one tree, each named by its dotted path into the scan's `counts`, as ffimap's `docs/schema.md` describes; a metric is a counter, or a combination of counters that schema allows: a partition's leaves summed, a share read against the record it cuts, or subtracted from it. `--sites ...` also lists where each named counter's increments are, and takes leaves only, such as `fn.unsafe.pub`; the workspace is named before it. The counters that recur: - `fn.unsafe.pub`, the public `unsafe fn`s, the crate's public unsafe surface, of which `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.pub` are those neither a trait nor a seam required; and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, the raw pointers in their signatures; - `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`, the raw pointers in public fields and in the signatures of public safe fns, together `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub`, the raw pointers on the safe public interface; and their `of_which.void` shares, the type-erased ones among them; - `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, the references to a cell, less their `of_which.self_in_ref_accessor` and `of_which.self_in_trait_impl` shares, the positions ffibox sanctions: references to C memory where a handle belongs, which assert `noalias`, `readonly` or validity over memory C may write; `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std`, the same of the raw C structs; and `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`, the borrows, slices and strings formed from a raw pointer, over bytes C must neither free nor change while they live; - `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`, each an unchecked assertion that a value may move to or be shared with another thread; - `raw_ptr.deref.wr` and `raw_ptr.deref.rd`, raw-pointer writes and reads, each a pointer the implementer vouches is non-null, aligned, live, initialized and unaliased by a live reference; and - `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`, the types that hold a raw pointer and tear it down or copy it by hand, and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}`, those that declare nothing about it. Each of these five also has a `.total`, the sum of its two leaves, which is no leaf for `--sites`. ffimap is neither complete nor sound: its sites are where review starts, not all it covers. It does not count the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, such as a reference or lifetime-annotated handle made from a raw pointer by `&*p`, `from_ptr`, `from_raw` or `from_raw_parts`, or changed by a `transmute`: those are found in the source. What follows is how ffimap serves each stage: each section names the skill and section it adds to, and states only what ffimap adds there. ## Binding and porting ### Binding › Safe boundary Before a batch lands, a scan with `--sites fn.unsafe.pub raw_ptr.field.pub raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub` lists the public `unsafe fn`s and the raw pointers on the safe public interface, and each of those sites that belongs to the batch's changeset and that a safe variant could replace is fixed. Its `--sites` also name the unsafe code outside both regions, `code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions`, another crate's macro expansions included, which the `unsafe_code` lint misses, and `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.pub` and `.priv`: outside the raw bindings, each of those sites in the batch's changeset is moved into its region. ## Accounting ### Accounting › Landing cells A batch's row in the dashboard's `Batches: safety audit` table is the change in each of the Safety audit's metrics, from a scan of the tip its landing rebased onto to a scan of the tree it lands. ### Accounting › API stability `ffimap api` measures a safe crate's consumer-facing API per C item, from rustdoc JSON, as its `docs/api.md` describes, read in full before its first use. A C item is the `::` of a `Wraps` or `Replaces` anchor, its surface every stand-in the anchor names and the handles and owners tied to it, each judged by the contract [`binding-types`](../../rust/binding/types/SKILL.md)' Safe layout section gives a consumer: the methods every form offers, its reborrows and dereferences, and the traits a consumer can use, never a form's raw access or seams. A batch generates the safe crate's rustdoc JSON on the tip its landing rebased onto and on the tree it lands, with a nightly whose `format_version` the tool supports, and ffibox's, with private items, for the contracts of the forms it defines: ```bash cargo + rustdoc -p --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json ffimap api diff .json .json --dep .json --items "" --format json ``` Each item comes out `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed` or `new`, with its anchor's move from `Wraps` to `Replaces` where a port made it. The batch's row in the dashboard's `Batches: API stability` table counts them over its worklist, and over the crate's unattributed public items, compared per module. ### Accounting › Records An unseeded scan of the unsafe and FFI surface is recorded at each batch's, wave's and the campaign's end, as `ffimap.json` in its artifact directory: a batch's in the run dir of the run that landed it, a wave's in its wave's dir, as `layout` spells it, and the campaign's in `crustify/artifacts/`. A module's end is the scan of the last wave of its `wrap` and `port` items. ## Reviewing ### Reviewing › Objectives A review locates the sites of its objectives with a scan, `--sites` with their counters, and keeps those in its workset: the code its commits add or change, or its modules and the types, trait impls and functions they name. - `unsafety`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`. - `contracts`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, whose `# Safety` obligations are evaluated. - `ub`: these smells first, in this order: 1. references into C memory: the references to a cell outside its sanctioned positions, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` less those shares, and to a raw C struct, `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, then `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`; 2. thread-safety claims, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`, checked against the C library's contract: a data race is reachable from safe code when the library does not allow what they assert; 3. the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, found in the source: unsound when the handle can outlive the owner of the memory or the point at which C frees or invalidates it; 4. raw pointers a consumer can set, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and `raw_ptr.field.pub`, with their `of_which.void` shares: unsound when a safe path dereferences or frees what the consumer passed or stored; 5. raw-pointer dereferences, `raw_ptr.deref.wr` then `raw_ptr.deref.rd`: first in the modules that also hold references into C memory, where a write may invalidate a reference, and outside a type's accessors; and 6. hand-written teardown and copies, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`. ## Audit ### Audit workflow › Worksets The audit's worksets are planned from a scan of the crate, run once each build configuration it audits is in place, with `--sites` over the counters of its objectives. A file outside every configuration scanned has no sites, and is planned from its source. For `ub`, the modules that hold the smells ffimap's review guidance lists for `ub` are reviewed first, in that order; for `contracts`, those that hold the crate's unsafe API and its justifications, the `contracts` counters above. The rest of the crate follows the smells. The modules are batched by their sites, and a module that is split keeps a type, trait impl or function with its sites in one batch. A site of `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop`, `.impl_clone`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send` or `.sync`, at either leaf, is a trait impl, named `Drop for `, `Clone for `, `Send for ` or `Sync for `. Each review runs the same scan over its own modules, so the sites are not passed on. --- name: ffibox description: "The library the campaign's Rust holds C memory through, in both directions: owners, handles, lifecycle policies, status conventions, callbacks and exports. Read before writing any wrapper, owner, lifecycle strategy, callable type or export, when judging a crate for adoption, and when testing or reviewing one." --- # ffibox ffibox is the library a campaign's Rust expresses C's ownership and lifetime conventions through, in both directions: memory C allocates, frees, copies, refcounts or locks, held from Rust behind a safe API, and memory Rust owns that C holds, calls or reads. Its primitives stand in for raw pointers and hand-written `Drop` impls wherever C aliases a value; what C does not alias is plain Rust. Its `README.md` is read in full before the first wrapper is written, and each section below names the documents under its `docs/` that its stage reads, also in full. Which primitive serves which C declaration, and how each is built, is those documents'. A representation ffibox cannot express is hand-written, as its `docs/hand-written.md` describes, with the same seam and safety-comment discipline. Its goals and non-goals, `docs/goals.md`, are what a change to ffibox is judged against, as [`evolution`](../../crustify/evolution/SKILL.md) describes. What follows is how ffibox serves each stage: each section names the skill and section it adds to, and states only what ffibox adds there. ## Planning ### Dependencies › Adopted crates A candidate crate's soundness is read against the hazards `docs/goals.md`'s G9 lists, each of which ffibox excludes from the campaign's own bindings: the crate qualifies where its safe API excludes them too, by whatever means it uses. ## Binding workflow ### Binding workflow › Rust tree The workspace depends on ffibox by path, on the checkout the host provides, which is on the campaign's working branch of it, `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }` in Crustify's image, so that each run records its revision among its task's `revisions`. The path is the checkout's canonical one, with no symbolic link on it, and a `[patch]` that redirects another source of ffibox names the same: compile-fail snapshots normalize a path dependency only where the compiler's paths match the dependency's canonical directory. ## Binding and porting Binding reads `docs/ownership.md`, `docs/borrows.md`, `docs/patterns.md`, `docs/vtables.md` and `docs/hand-written.md`; porting reads `docs/outbound.md` too. ### Binding types A type that stays interoperable with C is bound through ffibox's primitives wherever they apply, as `docs/ownership.md` and `docs/borrows.md` walk from its C declaration to them. ### Binding types › Safe layout While a type keeps its C layout, `define_ctype!` mints `Foo`, `FooRef<'a>` and `FooMut<'a>`, and its owners are aliases of ffibox's owners over the policy that names its lifecycle routines: `pub type FooBox = CBox;`, and `CArc` for `FooArc`. A value held inline that disposes its resources on drop is a `CVal`. ### Binding symbols › Functions A C routine's status convention becomes a `Result` through `status`, an object returned through an out-parameter a return value through `from_c_out` or `from_raw_out`, and C's iteration conventions iterators, as `docs/patterns.md` maps them. ### Binding symbols › Function pointers A function pointer's callable type is a `CCallback`, where C holds it for a call or a borrow, or a `CCallbackBox`, where C keeps it until it releases its context. Its Rust half is a closure, a `CClosure` or a `CPayload`, which C reaches through its trampoline; its C half is a C function with its context, a `CFn` or a `CFnBox`, which Rust calls, built only inside the crate through its `unsafe` constructor. A trampoline is the panic barrier, `callback::barrier`, which also guards an export's body. A struct of function pointers a library calls into, implemented by a Rust trait, is a `CTable` whose slots `impl_cvtable!` mints, over the binding's own `unsafe impl CVtable`, as `docs/vtables.md` describes; a table C implements is held as any other C object. A family of hooks that carries no context is trampolines over `callback::barrier`, not a table. ### Binding symbols › Lifecycle strategies Each lifecycle is held by the owner `docs/ownership.md` chooses for its shape, over the policy that names its routines; a policy with state, such as an allocator context, is held by `CBoxState`. content.content:
### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` wave 194 batch 7: module pass

The module pass, over api.c's whole module across its batches (`api.rs` and its `equiv`,
`ub_safe` and `unit_pub` files), for every objective with `fix`, and the wave's and the
module's end gates. `llhttp.rs`'s twelve units bound ahead were read, not reported on. It
files two findings, `+equiv` and `+misc`, both fixed.

- **equiv**: `llhttp_execute`'s export read a run of 0 bytes as `&[]`, whose address is
  `0x1`. A run of 0 bytes that ends a span the previous run left open, refused by the span's
  callback, so left `error_pos` at `0x1`, where api.c's `llhttp__internal_execute(parser,
  data, data + len)` leaves it at `data`. `git_http_parser_execute` subtracts `data` from it.
  libgit2's C calls `llhttp_finish` for an empty run, so it does not reach this. A reproducer
  runs the export beside api.c's body, with the exports linked in place of `api.c.o`, and
  exits 101. The export now reads any non-NULL `data` as its `len` bytes, an empty run
  included. The regression test is the gateway's `unit_priv`
  `llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data`.
- **misc**: `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence tests,
  which stay, also read their parsers through api.c's getters, its name functions and
  `llhttp_settings_init`. None of those has an export, so with `api.c.o` out of the archive
  `equiv` did not link even with api.c's own file retired (`rust-lld`: 23 undefined
  symbols, 10 of them from `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`). Batches 4 and 6 had left
  `equiv` out of their link checks as a whole. The nine tests that compare `llhttp.rs`'s
  accessors and maps with api.c's functions moved, unchanged, into an inline `getters` module
  of `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. So retiring that one file, with its `mod api;`, is
  api.c's whole equivalence retirement at the switch.

The retirement removes 21 `equiv` tests. The report maps each to the `unit_pub` tests that
keep what it established. Five new `unit_pub` tests keep what no unit test kept: what a
response read in pieces leaves the getters, an unnamed status, a request's method and a
`CONNECT`'s upgrade, an error located in sub-slices, a callback's own error read as unnamed,
and the type a setter sets deciding the next parse. A new gateway test,
`each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot`, checks that each of the 23 exports `llhttp.c`
calls by name reaches its own slot, which only the retiring `equiv` test did for all of them.
What no test keeps, and none needs once the C is gone: that each operation leaves the private
parser state byte for byte as C's did from six states, and that the lenient setters read any
nonzero `int` as true.

What held. The unsafe regions' justifications hold on every path: the table read, the slot
calls, the type byte, `reinit_keeping_context` and `stderr`, and `Settings`' `CZeroable`,
`Send` and `Sync`. Batch 6's corrected `set_settings_ptr`, `set_data` and `parser_mut`
contracts stand. The 31 exports are every api.c symbol the remaining C references:
`httpparser.c` (`llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`, `llhttp_get_error_pos`,
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`), `httpparser.h`'s macros (`llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`,
`llhttp_resume`, `llhttp_get_error_reason`) and `llhttp.c`'s 23 dispatchers. No C test,
`http.c` or other C file calls another. The exports keep what that C relies on: the error
position inside the run, the reason a `'static` C string, `llhttp_pause` safe from inside
`on_headers_complete`, and no unwind into C. `libgit2.so` keeps their symbols local
(`--exclude-libs`, `utf8.c`'s switch). No offline C test drives the HTTP client:
`tests/libgit2/core/features.c` only names the parser. So after the switch the exports are
checked by the gateway's eight `unit_priv` tests, which then always compile, by the safe API's
`unit_pub` and `ub_safe` tests, and by libgit2's `online` suites (`online::clone`,
`online::fetch`, `online::push` over HTTP), which the C baseline disables and need the network.

Gates, at 24 jobs, without BSan (the settings' `sanitizers` answer). On the tip `9124cc5a6`
(`end-gates` snapshot): plain passes the whole workspace (`lib` 854 and 1 ignored, `equiv`
553, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 137, `unit_pub` 156, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 92 and
387). ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known `compile_fail` snapshot and `CommitBuilder`
doctest. Miri passes every binary (`lib` 406, `equiv` 38, `ub_safe` 201, `unit_pub` 85,
`ub_unsafe` 19 passed, the rest marked). On this tree, `fmt` and `clippy --workspace
--all-targets` pass with warnings denied with the export feature off and on. On `b5eda0b43`'s tree (`end-gates`), plain passes the whole
workspace (`lib` 854 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 553, `unit_pub` 161, the rest as on the tip), and
ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known failures. Miri the changed binaries: `unit_pub` 85 and `equiv` 38 passed, the rest marked, and with
the feature on the gateway's 12, `each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot` among them. Each
new test marked `calls C` was run alone under Miri and stops at `llhttp__internal_init`.
With the exports linked in place of `api.c.o` (`crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>`, archive
copies of 211 objects named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`), and `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
retired in a scratch tree as the switch will retire it, the whole workspace passes on plain
(`lib` 861 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 137, `unit_pub` 161,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 92 and 387). ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known
failures. `nm` shows the 31 exports defined and no other api.c symbol.

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the tip and on this tree, read with `report.py` from
each scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. The totals
move from `47.26`% / `98.69`% to `47.24`% / `98.69`%; the C deltas but unit's are run-to-run
noise, since those suites run the same tests. Worklist: `api.rs` 187 of 187 lines, 39 of 39
functions, 226 of 227 regions; the gateway compiles out with the feature off. The new unit
tests take `llhttp.rs` from 289 to 291 of its 310 lines under the unit column. `api.c` keeps
267 of its 283 lines and 54 of 55 functions under `equiv`, `llhttp__debug` the one left. The
safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as batch 6's, the export feature on) differs from
the tip's only in test counters (`code.tests.loc.total` `+243`, which the Overview takes).
`ffimap api` against the tip (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's private rustdoc JSON): the 65
anchored keys are `kept`, the two private macro ports `missing`, and every unattributed module
`kept`. No raw binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. The `+unit` cell
counts the five `unit_pub` tests; the gateway's two compile out with the feature off.
Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's third switch, run by `modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch, after the merge of the working branch (`a4335ab7a`): `21c5c5f47`, and the fork's
`c54c0c180`. It followed the procedure of `utf8.c`'s and `opt.c`'s switches
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with their scripts unchanged. The export feature
`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` is deleted, so `api.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its
eight `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The remaining C calls the 31
exports: `transports/httpparser.c` calls `llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`,
`llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, `httpparser.h`'s macros, which
`httpclient.c` expands, call `llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume` and
`llhttp_get_error_reason`, and `llhttp.c`'s generated parser calls the 23 `llhttp__on_*`
dispatchers. The raw bindings of the eight functions stay and reach the exports. The dispatchers
have no header declaration and no raw binding. The 23 functions bound without an export go with
their allowlist entries: the seven getters, the three name functions, `llhttp_settings_init`,
`llhttp_reset`, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the ten lenient setters. Only api.c's equivalence
tests called them, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without them. Removing them changes the
crate's raw API, `sys::libgit2`, as the porting workflow's switch has it; the safe API does not
change. The types stay for the layouts `httpparser.c` and `llhttp.c` build and read.
`deps/llhttp/api.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as `integrate deps/llhttp/api.c`,
which is not pushed. `llhttp.h` stays for `llhttp.c`, `http.c` and the HTTP client.
`deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` globs its sources and is unchanged; its
`set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c …)` names the removed file, and CMake ignores
it. The module has no tied C test. The doc comment that counted nine functions C calls now says
eight.

The module's 21 `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
and its `mod api;`). Each calls C, api.c's own or `llhttp.c`'s parse through it, and carries the
Miri `calls C` marker, so none is carried over. The module pass (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc`
report) maps each to the unit tests that keep its behaviour. What none keeps is the
differential itself. The parser's private state was compared byte for byte with C's from six
states, and the lenient setters were shown to read any nonzero `int` as true. Once the C is gone,
nothing is left to compare with. `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs` stays: it compares
`llhttp.c`'s port with its C, whose parse now runs over the Rust dispatchers.

The Rust side landed before the variants were built: every variant's build runs
`rust-staticlib.sh`, which checks the committed bindings and compiles the gateway (proposal's
item 10). The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180` with
`build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 64. This
worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen3, and gen2 was left untouched. Each archive holds 210
objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and
`libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports and none of api.c's 23 other functions. `addr2line` puts
`llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`,
`git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same 907 symbols. It now
holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (proposal's item 9).

Gates, over gen3 from `end-gates` snapshots at 64 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
`lib` 901 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 101 and 397. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly
failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots, the six `checkout_*`,
`diff_parse_options_no_raw_conversion`, `odb_options_no_raw_conversion` and
`progress_callback_not_send`, and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). Neither printed a
sanitizer report. The gateway's eight tests pass on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, the first time
under TSan. Miri passes every binary: `lib` 441, `ub_safe` 212, `unit_pub` 141, `equiv` 38,
`ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The gateway's tests are among them: six pass, and
`llhttp_init_initialises_storage_and_stores_what_c_passes` and
`llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data` are marked `calls C`. The remaining C
tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443
passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the baseline's record. Under TSan, the
same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's lock-order inversions and races, and no case
fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and
coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and
glibc's `tzset` race, as at the two switches before. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.

No offline C test drives the HTTP client, and the baseline disables the online suites. So this
switch checked the exports through libgit2's own C over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost:
`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind an HTTP/1.1 front with persistent
connections, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` (proposal's item 11). The front frames each
response by its path: `Content-Length`, chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked
with chunk extensions, close-delimited, or a header block llhttp refuses. One remote asks for
Basic credentials. The variant's `git2` cloned `testrepo.git` and a three-commit repository of
the source revision's tree through the first three framings, each clone's refs, HEAD, checkout
and `fsck --connectivity-only` checked. It also ran four clones that fail: close-delimited ("could
not read refs from remote repository"), malformed ("http parser error: Invalid header token",
the reason read through `llhttp_get_error_reason`), 404 and 401. Through each of the first three
framings, `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` ran against the guarded
remote with `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`, as libgit2's CI runs `auth_clone_and_push`, and passed 23 with
1 skipped. Gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and
gen3's coverage variant gives it too: every outcome, every clone's refs, and the requests each
remote answered, by method, framing and status. No run printed a sanitizer report. On the
coverage variant, the run called 24 of the 31 exports, the chunk-extension dispatchers
included, and covered `api.rs`'s 128 of 175 lines and 31 of 44 functions. The seven it never
calls are `on_url` and `on_method` and their `_complete`s, which only a request parse calls,
`on_reset` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, which need pipelined or upgraded messages, and
`llhttp_finish`, which libgit2 calls only when the socket ends inside a body. The gateway's
`unit_priv` tests call six of them: `each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot` calls every
dispatcher and `llhttp_finish_returns_cs_codes` calls `llhttp_finish`. None calls
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, whose body is `ParserMut::resume_after_upgrade` in a `barrier`;
`unit_pub`'s `resume_after_upgrade_clears_only_an_upgrades_pause` tests that method. The results are kept in the run dir
(`http-gate-results.txt`), for the switches of `http.c` and `llhttp.c` to compare with.

`c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as `package-gate-procedure` has it, with the workspace's
Git patch of ffibox, as at `opt.c`'s switch. It has 695 files, `api.c` out, and builds alone in
bundled mode, where `llhttp.c`'s dispatchers resolve to the Rust. Its `lib` tests: 843 pass, the
gateway's eight among them. The other 58 need the fixture repositories of `c/tests/resources`,
as at the two switches before.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's, and the C figures lose `api.c`'s 283
lines. This run did not measure the workspace's coverage. What this switch shows the procedure
lacks is added to `crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure` (items 10 to 13). The review
reproducer that enables the deleted feature (`wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`)
is left as it is, reproducing at the commit its report names. Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c` wave 197 batch 0: the module's `port`

http.c's whole `port`, the `symbol` route of waves 197, 198 and 199 folded into one batch on
wave 197's branch: 5 items in `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.rs`, each a method of the parser's
handles over `llhttp.rs`'s accessors, so no item reaches the raw struct: every field the five
read or write has an accessor, the flag words through `flags_raw` and `lenient_flags_raw`, read
against the raw bindings' `F_*` and `LENIENT_*` constants. `fn::llhttp_message_needs_eof` and
`fn::llhttp_should_keep_alive` are `ParserRef::message_needs_eof()` and `should_keep_alive()`,
`bool`s. `fn::llhttp__before_headers_complete` is `ParserMut::before_headers_complete()`, which
cannot fail and returns nothing, C's `0` reporting nothing. `fn::llhttp__after_headers_complete`
only reads the parser, though C takes it non-const, so it is
`ParserRef::after_headers_complete() -> Result<Body, InvalidTransferEncoding>`: `Body` is the
five codes the generated parser goes on from (`Empty`, `Upgrade`, `Chunked`, `Length`,
`UntilEof`), and `InvalidTransferEncoding` the sixth, a request whose `Transfer-Encoding` does
not end with `chunked`, which the parser refuses with `HPE_INVALID_TRANSFER_ENCODING` (its
`errno()`, and `Display` gives llhttp's reason). `fn::llhttp__after_message_complete` is
`ParserMut::after_message_complete() -> bool`, the keep-alive it settles before marking the
parser `HTTP_FINISH_SAFE` and clearing its flags. The type and method are compared as llhttp's
enums, which an unnamed byte never equals, as C's `==` has it; the version as llhttp reads it,
HTTP/1.1 or later only with both major and minor above zero, so `HTTP/2.0` keeps alive only
with `Connection: keep-alive`, kept and documented. `enm::llhttp_flags`, which `llhttp.c` owns,
is not wrapped: its constants are read from the raw bindings, as `llhttp.rs` reads the lenient
flags. The analysis's findings are in the ownership store, the five `parser` arguments borrowed
for the call and not kept, the hooks' `p` and `endp` never read.

The gateway gains 4 exports under `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c`, declared anew in
`Cargo.toml`: the three hooks, which `llhttp.c` calls, and `llhttp_should_keep_alive`, which
libgit2's HTTP client calls (`httpparser.h`'s `git_http_parser_keep_alive`, in
`httpclient.c`'s `on_headers_complete`). `llhttp_message_needs_eof` has no C caller outside
http.c, so it has no export and leaves with http.c's C, as its raw binding will. Each export is
`barrier`ed and aborts on a panic, none of the four having a failure a panic could report.
`llhttp_should_keep_alive` is checked against its raw binding; the hooks, which no header
declares, against a `Hook` function-pointer type transcribed from `llhttp.c`'s prototypes,
and `equiv` declares them in an `extern` block of its own
(`crustify/evolution/exports-without-a-header-declaration`, with this evidence). The raw
bindings gain `llhttp_flags` (`F_*`), `llhttp_message_needs_eof` and `llhttp_should_keep_alive`.
The gateway's `cfg` is the attribute right above `mod ffi_export`, after the region's
multi-line `expect`: in the other order `build.rs`'s `gateway_lines` reads the gateway as a
switched module's, as it read api.c's before its switch
(`crustify/evolution/gateway-feature-across-a-multiline-attribute`, with a reproducer).

The link check of the task message ran on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`: private builds under
`crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` whose archive copy lacks `deps/llhttp/http.c.o` (209
objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, over a scratch tree with `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs`
retired, the feature on. The archive holds two `http.c.o`, `transports/http.c`'s first, so the
second was removed (`ar dN 2`), `nm` showing the one left defines `git_smart_subtransport_http`
(`crustify/evolution/export-link-check`, with this evidence). Every binary linked, `equiv`
included: on `plain`, `lib` 907 (the gateway's four `unit_priv` tests among them), `equiv` 532,
`ub_safe` 798, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 230, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 106 and 397; on
`asan-ubsan` the same but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots (9 of 197) and
`CommitBuilder` doctest, with no sanitizer report. `nm` shows the four exports defined, at
`http.rs`, and no `llhttp_message_needs_eof`. The variants' `git2` and `libgit2_tests` were then
relinked from their `build.ninja` edges without `deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o` and
with the crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` ran
over them on `plain`, `asan-ubsan` and `coverage`: each `results.txt` is identical to the one
api.c's switch recorded over gen3's C (`modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1`),
every clone, failure, suite tally and request alike, with no sanitizer report. On `coverage`,
the run reaches all five: the four exports from C, all but their abort-on-panic paths, and `message_needs_eof` through
`should_keep_alive` and `after_headers_complete`. It covers `http.rs`'s 109 of 150 lines and 18
of 25 functions, `after_headers_complete`'s codes 0, 2, 3 and 4 among them. A response never
makes the request's refusal, the upgrade or the lenient paths, nor a 1xx's early returns.

Tests: 2 `unit_priv` (the codes the parser switches on, `HTTP_FINISH_SAFE`'s byte) and 4 more in
the gateway's region, under the feature (each export as C calls it, over parsers Rust builds:
what it reads and writes, and its `int`), 12 `unit_pub` (each function over zeroed parsers
through the setters, every flag word of a request for `message_needs_eof`, then over the states

### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` integration: the switch from C

`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` on the module's branch, after the merge of the
working branch (`6d823f4d7`): `f68ea8660`, and the fork's `f57e1a616`. It followed
`utf8.c`'s procedure (`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with its scripts unchanged.
The export feature `ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` is deleted, so `opt.rs`'s gateway compiles from
now on, and its six `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The CLI's
remaining C calls the five exports `cli_opt_parser_init`, `cli_opt_parser_next`,
`cli_opt_parse`, `cli_opt_foreach` and `cli_opt_status_fprint`: `main.c`, the `cmd_*.c`
commands, `common.c` and `opt_usage.c`. Their raw bindings stay and reach the exports. The
module binds no function without an export, so no allowlist entry goes. The types stay for the
layouts that C builds and reads. `src/cli/opt.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as
`integrate src/cli/opt.c`, which is not pushed. `opt.h` stays for `common.h`. The module has no
tied C test. The exports are a private module's, so the crate's API does not change.

The module's 16 `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/src/cli/opt.rs`,
and `tests/equiv/src/cli.rs` with it). Two of them call no C: `usage_flags_match_the_c_constants`
and `parse_flags_match_the_c_constants` compare `Usage`'s and `ParseFlags`' bits with `opt.h`'s
constants through the raw bindings. No unit test kept that, and the CLI's spec tables, which
stay C, set those bits, so both move to `unit_pub` as `usage_flags_keep_their_c_values` and
`parse_flags_keep_their_c_values`. The kinds' and statuses' constants were already in
`unit_priv`. The behaviour no unit test keeps is the differential itself. The C parser's
outcomes, parser states, argument orders and variables were compared step by step with the
port's over the `equiv` corpus: two spec tables, both styles and every command line of the
corpus. `Parser::new` was compared byte for byte, padding included, with `cli_opt_parser_init`'s
parser. The unit tests assert the port's results case by case, as C gave them, and the
relinked CLI below checks the whole path. Once the C is gone, nothing is left to compare with.

The CLI's link unit needed no change of its own. `utf8.c`'s `SelectRust.cmake` already links
the Rust library into the CLI, which takes libgit2's objects statically, and the crate's
default features include `git2`. So `rust-staticlib.sh`'s library carries the CLI's exports once
the feature is gone. The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen2` from `f57e1a616` with
`build-variants.sh`, at 10 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 48. This
worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen2, and gen1 was left untouched. Each archive holds 211
objects where gen1's held 212, `opt.c.o` gone. Each variant's `git2` defines the five exports as
global Rust symbols, where gen1's were the C's local ones. Each passed its smoke test
(`util_tests -sutf8`, `git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same
907 symbols. It now holds 6337 local Rust functions where gen1's held 2608, and imports about 75
more glibc functions. It calls none of the CLI's exports: the linker takes whole members of the
dev-profile library and collects no unused sections (proposal's item 9).

Gates, over gen2 from `end-gates` snapshots at 48 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
`lib` 887 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 528, `ub_safe` 774, `ub_unsafe` 127, `unit_pub` 141,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 85 and 388. ASan+UBSan passes it but for the known nightly
failures, the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). On
`cd7b59007`, TSan failed one more test: the gateway's
`the_status_message_describes_a_failed_parse`, which had never run under TSan, since it
compiled only with the feature. It read the export's `errno` after closing its memory stream,
and TSan's `fclose`/`free` interceptors leave `EBADF` there. It now reads `errno` right after the
call (`f68ea8660`). `lib`, the only binary that test compiles into, then passed whole on plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan (887 and 1 ignored). Miri passes every binary: `lib` 429, `ub_safe` 205,
`unit_pub` 105, `equiv` 38, `ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The fix changed only a test that
Miri ignores. The remaining C tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. The
Rust there was built from the switch's tree, and the fix touches only `#[cfg(test)]` code.
Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443 passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each
the baseline's record. Under TSan, the same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's
lock-order inversions and races, and no case fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes
both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports
alone, 49 lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race, as at `utf8.c`'s switch. No C test reaches the CLI, so its exports were checked
by the module pass's comparison (`wave-186/batch-7/run-1`'s `cli-smoke.py`), gen1's `git2`
beside gen2's, over its 66 command lines. On plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan alike, 62 are the same
and 4 differ: the module's recorded departures, the bare `-` three times and the literal `--`'s
reordering. Neither side gave a sanitizer report. Each of gen2's 66 outcomes is the module
pass's relinked CLI's, but for three (`cat-file -p HEAD`, `cat-file commit HEAD`, `blame f1`)
that differ only in the scratch commit's date and id. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.

`c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as `package-gate-procedure` has it: 696 files, `opt.c`
out. It built alone in bundled mode only once its manifest also took the workspace's Git patch
of ffibox. Without it, `glibc-bindings`' Git ffibox and the crate's path ffibox are two crates,
and the gateway's `FileRef::from_ptr` does not compile (E0599). That evidence is added to the
proposal. Its `lib` tests: 829 pass, the 39 of `cli::opt` among them. The other 58 need the
fixture repositories of `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's, and the C figures lose `opt.c`'s 403
lines. This run did not measure coverage. What this switch shows the procedure lacks is added to
`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure` (items 5 to 9). The two review reproducers that
enable the deleted feature (`wave-186/batch-6` and `batch-7`) are left as they are, reproducing
at the commits their reports name. Usage cells are the assistant's.

configuration and links none of its C. It instruments the Rust as `cargo-variant.sh` does.
`nm` shows that the library defines only the Rust, the three exports and the crate's
`__extern` wrappers, and no libgit2 C. Every other campaign build leaves the library out of
its link, matched by canonical path, so that no binary holds the Rust twice. BSan has no
`cargo bsan rustc`, so a stand-in for the cargo it runs turns its `build` into `rustc
--crate-type staticlib`. The BSan runtime its driver bundles is removed from the copy, since
the variant's C link links it.

The variants were rebuilt as a new generation, `crustify/builds.gen1`, with
`crustify/scripts/build-variants.sh`, and this worktree's `crustify/builds` links to it.
`crustify/builds` itself, which three batches were using, was left untouched. Each variant is
configured from the generation's own `c`, a detached worktree of the fork at `1b37e3d08`, so
that the build outlives this worktree and the base checkout's next moves (`build.json`
version 7). Each archive holds 212 objects, where the previous generation's held 213:
`utf8.c.o` is gone. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`). In every
variant, `utf8proc_utf8class` is absent from the C test executables, which take
`git_utf8_iterate` from the Rust; in `libgit2.so` it is a local symbol.

Gates on `012d1d34c`, over gen1, from `end-gates` snapshots at 24 jobs. The workspace is
formatted, and `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes
the whole workspace: `lib` 848 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 528, `ub_safe` 763, `ub_unsafe` 120,
`unit_pub` 84, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 76 and 378. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for
the known nightly failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest
(E0624). Miri passes every binary: `lib` 400, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 49,
`ub_unsafe` 19, the rest marked. The remaining C tests ran over the link with the Rust,
through `crustify/scripts/c-tests.sh`. It runs `build.json`'s `ctest` command, then every
suite alone as the baseline did, and compares the result with `c-baseline.json`. Plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443 passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the
baseline's record. Under TSan, the same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's
lock-order inversions and races, and no case fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest`
passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those
reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race. BSan was rebuilt and not
run, as the settings' `sanitizers` answer has it. `c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as
`package-gate-procedure` has it. The package has 697 files, `utf8.c` out and
`SelectRust.cmake` in, and builds alone in bundled mode. Its `libgit2.pc`'s
`Requires.private` also needs the side campaigns' installs on `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, beside
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`. Its `lib` tests link, `path.c`'s `next_hfs_char` calling the Rust export.
790 pass, among them the module's; the other 58 need the fixture repositories of
`c/tests/resources`, which the package leaves out.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's: `utf8.c` is in no build, and the C
figures lose its 71 lines. This run did not measure coverage. The procedure this switch
worked out, which every later switch repeats, is proposed for the spec
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`). That libgit2's switch removes a file and no
CMake line is a lesson. Usage cells are the assistant's.

usage: end-gates [-h] [--logs LOGS] [--stages STAGES] [--rev REV |
                 --working-tree] [--label LABEL] [--package PACKAGE]
                 [--runner RUNNER] [--link LINK] [--skip-file SKIP_FILE]
                 [--stage-env STAGE_ENV] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                 [--parallel PARALLEL] [--nightly NIGHTLY]
                 [tree]

end-gates: run a wave's or a module's end gates over a snapshot of a tree.

    end-gates <tree> --logs <dir> [--stages plain,asan-ubsan,tsan,miri,bsan]
              [--rev <rev> | --working-tree] [--package <name>] [--runner <cmd>]
              [--link <path>]... [--skip-file <file>] [--stage-env <stage>:<K>=<V>]...
              [--timeout <seconds>] [--parallel <n>] [--nightly <toolchain>]

The gates of testing-gates' Regressions section, run exactly so:

1. The tree's commit (`--rev`, HEAD by default), or its working tree with
   `--working-tree`, is copied to a snapshot, `<tree>/crustify/tmp/gates-<label>`, so that
   work goes on in the tree while the gates run. Each submodule, and each `--link` path
   (such as the variants' builds dir), is symlinked from the tree into it, and the snapshot
   is made a git repository, since a test may discover the repository it runs in.
2. Each skip of `--skip-file` is checked against its test binary's `--list` before any
   stage runs: a skip that names no test, or that would also skip another, since libtest
   skips by substring, fails the run.
3. The stages run in the order given:
   - a variant (`plain` and each sanitizer but `bsan`): the workspace's tests,
     `<runner> <variant> test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, with that stage's skips;
   - `miri`: the package's test binaries built once on the pinned nightly, then one
     `cargo miri test` per test binary, side by side, each skipping `compile_fail`;
   - `bsan`: the test binaries built once, then one invocation per test binary, side by
     side, each under `--timeout`, with that stage's skips.
4. Each run writes `<logs>/<stage>[-<binary>].log`; `<logs>/summary.json` and
   `summary.txt` record each run's command, exit status, duration, test-result lines and
   failed tests. A run that exceeds its timeout reports `timed_out`.

The skip file holds one skip per line, `<stage> <binary> <exact test name>`, the binary
being `lib` or an integration test's name; `#` starts a comment. A variant stage's skips
apply to every binary of the workspace.

The job count is the environment's: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` for builds, `RUST_TEST_THREADS` for
each binary's tests, as concurrency describes. The exit status is 0 when every run
passed, 1 when any failed, and 2 when the run could not start.

Standard library only.

positional arguments:
  tree

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --logs LOGS           the dir each run's log and the summary go to
  --stages STAGES       comma-separated, run in this order (default:
                        plain,asan-ubsan,tsan,miri,bsan)
  --rev REV             the commit to snapshot (default: HEAD)
  --working-tree        snapshot the working tree, tracked and untracked files
                        git keeps
  --label LABEL         the snapshot's name under crustify/tmp (default: the
                        rev)
  --package PACKAGE     the package whose test binaries run per binary
                        (default: the workspace's root package)
  --runner RUNNER       the command that runs cargo against a variant, given
                        the variant first (default: crustify/scripts/cargo-
                        variant.sh, from the snapshot)
  --link LINK           a path git leaves out, symlinked from the tree
                        (repeatable); submodules are linked always
  --skip-file SKIP_FILE
                        lines of `<stage> <binary> <test name>`
  --stage-env STAGE_ENV
                        <stage>:<K>=<V>, set for that stage's runs
                        (repeatable)
  --timeout TIMEOUT     seconds each BSan binary may run (default: 3600)
  --parallel PARALLEL   test binaries run side by side (default: all)
  --nightly NIGHTLY     Miri's toolchain (default: the workspace's `nightly`
                        key, else the rust-toolchain file's)
#!/bin/bash
# Drive libgit2's HTTP client through a variant's own C, over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost
# (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch, for a module whose exports
# the HTTP client reaches, which no offline C test does; crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure).
#
#   http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds.gen<n>/<variant>, with its `git2` and
# `libgit2_tests`; nothing is written into it. Two remotes are started from
# crustify/scripts/http-remote.py over scratch repositories under <out dir>/remotes, one open
# and one asking for Basic credentials (foo:bar), each serving every framing it offers
# (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited, malformed):
#
# 1. the variant's `git2 clone` of testrepo.git (c/tests/resources) and of a three-commit
#    repository of the generation's c/ tree at a fixed commit, through the Content-Length and
#    chunked framings, and clones that fail: through the close-delimited framing, which
#    libgit2 does not read to its end, through a response llhttp refuses, of a missing
#    repository (404), and of the guarded remote without credentials (401); each clone's exit
#    status, refs, HEAD, checked-out tree and `git fsck --connectivity-only` outcome, or its
#    error;
# 2. the variant's `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials`, libgit2's own
#    C tests of a push and a clone over GITTEST_REMOTE_URL, against the guarded remote with
#    foo:bar, through the Content-Length and chunked framings: its TAP tally.
#
# <out dir>/results.txt is one line per case, free of times, ports and paths, so that two
# generations' results compare with `diff`; every process's output is kept beside it, and each
# line counts the sanitizer reports that process printed (`reports=`). The exit status is 0
# when every clone that should succeed did and every suite passed, 1 otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
c=$(cd -P "$d/../c" && pwd) || { echo "http-gate.sh: no generation c/ beside $d" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$d/git2" ] && [ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] || { echo "http-gate.sh: $d has no git2 or libgit2_tests" >&2; exit 2; }
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
# big.git's tree: the campaign's source revision, which every generation's c/ holds.
big_tip=0551dfd4a
framings=(length chunked chunked-ext)
status=0
results=$out/results.txt
: >"$results"
reports() { grep -cE 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer|ERROR: AddressSanitizer|ERROR: LeakSanitizer|runtime error:' "$@" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'; }

# The remotes' repositories.
r=$out/remotes
mkdir -p "$r/open" "$r/guarded"
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/open/testrepo.git"
# big.git: the source revision's tree as three commits, the second removing src/ and the
# third restoring it, each with a fixed author and date, so that its ids are every run's.
mkdir -p "$r/src"
git -C "$c" archive "$big_tip" | tar -x -C "$r/src"
(
  cd "$r/src" && git init -q -b main . &&
    export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=crustify GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu \
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=crustify GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu &&
    git add -A && git commit -q -m tree &&
    git rm -q -r src && git commit -q -m 'without src' &&
    git revert --no-edit HEAD >/dev/null
)
git clone -q --bare "$r/src" "$r/open/big.git"
rm -rf "$r/src"
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do git init -q --bare "$r/guarded/push-$f.git"; done
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/guarded/testrepo.git"

pids=()
trap 'kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT

being `lib` or an integration test's name; `#` starts a comment. A variant stage's skips
apply to every binary of the workspace.

passed, 1 when any failed, and 2 when the run could not start.

#!/bin/bash
# Drive libgit2's HTTP client through a variant's own C, over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost
# (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch, for a module whose exports
# the HTTP client reaches, which no offline C test does; crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure).
#
#   http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds.gen<n>/<variant>, with its `git2` and
# `libgit2_tests`; nothing is written into it. Two remotes are started from
# crustify/scripts/http-remote.py over scratch repositories under <out dir>/remotes, one open
# and one asking for Basic credentials (foo:bar), each serving every framing it offers
# (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited, malformed):
#
# 1. the variant's `git2 clone` of testrepo.git (c/tests/resources) and of a three-commit
#    repository of the generation's c/ tree at a fixed commit, through the Content-Length and
#    chunked framings, and clones that fail: through the close-delimited framing, which
#    libgit2 does not read to its end, through a response llhttp refuses, of a missing
#    repository (404), and of the guarded remote without credentials (401); each clone's exit
#    status, refs, HEAD, checked-out tree and `git fsck --connectivity-only` outcome, or its
#    error;
# 2. the variant's `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials`, libgit2's own
#    C tests of a push and a clone over GITTEST_REMOTE_URL, against the guarded remote with
#    foo:bar, through the Content-Length and chunked framings: its TAP tally.
#
# <out dir>/results.txt is one line per case, free of times, ports and paths, so that two
# generations' results compare with `diff`; every process's output is kept beside it, and each
# line counts the sanitizer reports that process printed (`reports=`). The exit status is 0
# when every clone that should succeed did and every suite passed, 1 otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
c=$(cd -P "$d/../c" && pwd) || { echo "http-gate.sh: no generation c/ beside $d" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$d/git2" ] && [ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] || { echo "http-gate.sh: $d has no git2 or libgit2_tests" >&2; exit 2; }
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
# big.git's tree: the campaign's source revision, which every generation's c/ holds.
big_tip=0551dfd4a
framings=(length chunked chunked-ext)
status=0
results=$out/results.txt
: >"$results"
reports() { grep -cE 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer|ERROR: AddressSanitizer|ERROR: LeakSanitizer|runtime error:' "$@" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'; }

# The remotes' repositories.
r=$out/remotes
mkdir -p "$r/open" "$r/guarded"
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/open/testrepo.git"
# big.git: the source revision's tree as three commits, the second removing src/ and the
# third restoring it, each with a fixed author and date, so that its ids are every run's.
mkdir -p "$r/src"
git -C "$c" archive "$big_tip" | tar -x -C "$r/src"
(
  cd "$r/src" && git init -q -b main . &&
    export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=crustify GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu \
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=crustify GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu &&
    git add -A && git commit -q -m tree &&
    git rm -q -r src && git commit -q -m 'without src' &&
    git revert --no-edit HEAD >/dev/null
)
git clone -q --bare "$r/src" "$r/open/big.git"
rm -rf "$r/src"
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do git init -q --bare "$r/guarded/push-$f.git"; done
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/guarded/testrepo.git"

pids=()
trap 'kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/open" "$out/open.port" --log "$out/open.log" 2>"$out/open.err" &
pids+=($!)
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/guarded" "$out/guarded.port" --auth foo:bar --log "$out/guarded.log" 2>"$out/guarded.err" &

guarded=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/guarded.port")
