# A port batch runs its module's tests with its exports linked in place of its C

Status: `open`.

## Signal

One procedure repeated by hand, which no gate runs. `testing-gates`' Regressions section
has a `port` batch check and lint the safe crate with its module's export feature on,
"which compiles the module's gateway without linking it", and compare each export's
signature with its raw binding. Nothing runs the gateway before the module's switch: every
gate builds with the feature off, and the `testing` skill puts an export's tests "with the
stage that removes the form", which compile only under the feature. A gateway that
compiles, and has C's signature, but writes the wrong out-parameter, reads past its size or
mishandles a NULL, passes every gate until the switch rebuilds the variants, when the C
tests that remain are the first to call it.

## Evidence

- `wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, the crate's first gateway) ran, "as a
  scratch check, not a gate", its tests with the exports linked in place of the archive's
  `utf8.o` (its dashboard notes).
- `wave-229/batch-1/run-1`, its module pass, did it again, by hand: a private build dir under
  `crustify/tmp/` whose entries link to the variant's, but for a copy of its static archive
  without the module's objects (`ar d libcrustify.a utf8.c.o`), named by
  `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`; then `cargo-variant.sh <variant> test --workspace --features
  ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, which passed but for the known
  nightly failures, `nm` showing no `utf8proc_utf8class` and `next_hfs_char` calling Rust.
  It also relinked the variant's C test executables (`libgit2_tests`, `util_tests`) from
  their `build.ninja` edges, without `src/util/CMakeFiles/util.dir/utf8.c.o` and with the
  crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on: `-sutf8`, and `-spath -sdiff -sindex
  -scheckout -srefs`, gave the stock binaries' results (825 passed, 22 skipped). A
  `util_tests` input list holds two `utf8.c.o`, the module's and its C test's, so removing
  by file name alone would drop the test: the procedure must name the object's path.
- The module pass added the gateway's own `unit_priv` tests, which compile only under the
  feature, and ran them by hand with it on, under Miri too.
- `wave-186/batch-5/run-1` and `wave-186/batch-6/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) ran the
  module's `equiv` tests the same way, by hand, against a copy of the archive without
  `opt.c.o`; those tests compare the C with the Rust, so with the exports linked they compare
  the exports with the native API, and they are retired with the C at the switch.
- `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, found the gateway with no test of its own and two
  defects that only the export's callers reach. Its gateway tests, written after `main.c`,
  `cmd_hash_object.c` and `common.c`, ran with the feature on against the private build and
  under Miri, where the feature also compiles: Miri reported
  `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`, a `char **` the export stored for C
  that a later unique reborrow invalidated, which no gate could reach, since every gate builds
  with the feature off. The module's remaining C is an executable, the CLI, which no C test
  runs (`modules.json`'s `tests` is empty, and no suite under `c/tests` reaches `src/cli`), so
  the switch's C-test gate checks nothing of these exports. The pass relinked the variant's
  `git2` from its `build.ninja` edge, without `src/cli/CMakeFiles/git2_cli.dir/opt.c.o` and
  with the crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on, and ran it and the stock `git2`
  over 66 command lines in scratch repositories: 62 alike, the 4 others the parser's recorded
  departures from the C. The procedure is recorded for this target as a lesson
  (`crustify/LESSONS.md`, "A `git2` module's exports are checked through the CLI").

- `wave-194/batch-4/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/api.c`, its last `port` batch) ran it by hand again,
  as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`: private build dirs under
  `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` linking to the variant's entries, with a copy of
  `libcrustify.a` less `api.c.o` (211 objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, and the tests
  run with `--features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`. Two things the procedure must say came
  out of it. First, not every test binary can link: the module's `equiv` binary calls 19 of
  api.c's functions that no remaining C calls and that therefore have no export
  (`llhttp_get_type`, the lenient setters, `llhttp_reset`, …), so it fails to link
  (`undefined symbol`), by design, since it compares with that C; the check runs the other
  binaries and the doctests, and the undefined symbols of `equiv` are the list of the module's
  unexported functions, every one of which should be api.c's own. Second, a test outside
  `equiv` that calls such a function through its raw binding fails to link too, and would
  fail at the switch: `ub_unsafe`'s llhttp fixtures called `llhttp_settings_init`, which the
  batch replaced with the zeroed table it makes. The rest passed (`lib` 858 with the gateway's
  six tests, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 156, doctests 92 and 387; under
  ASan+UBSan the same but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder`
  doctest), `nm` showing the exports defined and api.c's other symbols absent.

- `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, api.c's module pass, found that leaving `equiv` out of the check
  is itself a gap. `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence
  tests (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`), which stay, also called 10 of api.c's
  unexported functions, so retiring api.c's own equivalence file at the switch would still
  have left `equiv` unlinked
  (`misc/llhttp-equiv-tests-call-api-c-functions-without-exports`). `rust-lld` lists only
  20 undefined symbols by default, so the full list needs its `--error-limit=0`. The
  pass moved those tests into api.c's file, then ran the check over a scratch tree with that
  file retired, as the switch will: `equiv` linked, 532 passing on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and
  TSan. So the check must link `equiv` too, with only the module's own equivalence files
  retired, and fail on any undefined symbol it references from another module's file.

- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`, its whole `port`) ran the check by hand
  again, as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, over a scratch tree with its
  own equivalence file retired: every binary linked, `equiv` included (532), and passed but
  for the known nightly failures under ASan+UBSan. Removing the module's object by name would
  have removed the wrong one: the archive holds two `http.c.o` members,
  `src/libgit2/transports/http.c`'s (the 154th) and `deps/llhttp/http.c`'s (the 168th), and
  `ar d libcrustify.a http.c.o` deletes the first; the batch used `ar dN 2` and checked with
  `nm` that the member left defines `git_smart_subtransport_http`. So the script must take
  the module's objects by their `build.ninja` paths, as the `util_tests` evidence above found
  for a link's inputs, and pick an archive member by position, never by its base name alone.
  It also relinked the variants' `git2` and `libgit2_tests` from their `build.ninja` edges,
  without `deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o` and with the crate's static library
  built with the feature on, and ran `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` over them on `plain`,
  `asan-ubsan` and `coverage`, the module's only C callers being the HTTP client and
  `llhttp.c`, which no offline C test reaches.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, the export checks of a `port` batch, with a
script beside it, as `authoring` places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by
its `--help`: given a variant and the module's objects, as `build.ninja` names them, it
makes the private build dir with an archive lacking them, runs the workspace's tests with
the module's export feature on against it, and, where the target builds C test
executables, relinks them against the crate's static library in place of the module's
objects and runs the suites tied to the module and to the modules that call its exports.

The script also runs the gateway's own tests under Miri with the export feature on, which
Miri's builds allow before the switch since they link no C, and, where the module's remaining
C callers are executables that no C test runs, names that check as the gap it is: an export
whose only C callers are executables is checked by its gateway tests alone, which `testing`'s
UB tests section would have written after those callers, or by a relink of the executables
compared with the stock ones over the inputs the target documents.

## Change

Not made: a script and a new gate want their own review, and the module's integration,
right after this pass, exercises the same link through the target's build system. The
section would say that a `port` batch, and its module pass, run the check on `plain` and
`asan-ubsan`, and that a module's switch still runs the C tests over the actual build.

## Validation

To be run: the script on `wave-229`'s tree, passing, and failing when the gateway's
`bytes()` reads one byte past `str_len` (which the module pass's tests catch under Miri) or
when `git_utf8_iterate` leaves `*out` unwritten on a refusal.

## Review

Pending.
# build.rs reads a gateway as switched when a multi-line attribute follows its `cfg`

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A defect, worked around. `build.rs`'s `gateway_lines` finds each `mod ffi_export` of `src/`
and the export feature gating it, which `gateways` and `export_dynamic_symbols` read: a
gateway with no feature is a switched module's, which the `system` feature refuses to link
an install beside, and whose `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` items every binary exports dynamically;
a gated one counts only when its feature is on. It takes the feature from a `#[cfg(feature =
"ffi-export-…")]` line and keeps it across the attribute lines after it, but resets it on
any line that neither starts with `#[` nor `//`. The second line of a multi-line attribute,
such as the region's own `#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = …\n)]`, the toolchain's
form for a region that takes the lint back, is such a line, so a gateway written as the
conventions have it, its `cfg` first, is read as having no feature: as a switched module's,
whether or not the feature is on.

## Evidence

- The reproducer below, from `wave-197/batch-0/run-1`, transcribes `gateway_lines` line for
  line. On a gateway written `cfg`
  then a multi-line `expect`, it reads no feature (`[None]`); with the `cfg` right above the
  `mod`, it reads `DEPS_LLHTTP_HTTP_C`. On `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs` at `b3d6b9b37`
  (`wave-194/batch-4/run-1`, before api.c's switch), whose gateway was gated so, it reads
  `[None]`: from that batch to the switch, a `system` build would have refused, naming
  `api.rs` as switched, and every build in shared mode would have passed
  `-Wl,--export-dynamic-symbol=` for api.c's 31 exports with the feature off, whose names
  the C defined.
- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`) wrote its gateway with the `cfg` right
  above `mod ffi_export`, after the `expect`, with a comment saying why.

## Destination

The campaign's `build.rs` (`gateway_lines`), which the `bindgen` skill's Build modes
section specifies: a gateway's feature is the `cfg` among the attributes of its `mod`,
wherever it stands among them.

## Change

Not made: `build.rs` is the bindings', and not a translator's to change. In
`gateway_lines`, track an attribute until its brackets close, so that the lines inside a
multi-line attribute neither set nor reset the gate:

```rust
// in the loop, before the `cfg` match:
if attr_depth > 0 {
    attr_depth += braces_of(t, '[', ']');
    continue;
}
if t.starts_with("#[") && braces_of(t, '[', ']') > 0 {
    attr_depth = braces_of(t, '[', ']');
    continue;
}
```

with `braces_of` counting the opening less the closing brackets, as `braces` counts braces.
A regression test of `gateway_lines` over both orders, the reproducer's two cases, keeps it.

## Reproducer

```python
"""build.rs's gateway_lines, line for line: the feature it reads for each `mod ffi_export`."""
def gateways(text):
    gate = None; out = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        t = line.strip()
        if t.startswith('#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-') and t.endswith('")]'):
            gate = t[len('#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-'):-3].upper().replace('-', '_')
        elif t.startswith('mod ffi_export') or t.startswith('pub mod ffi_export'):
            out.append(gate); gate = None
        elif not t.startswith('#[') and not t.startswith('//') and t:
            gate = None
    return out
cfg_first = '#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c")]\n#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = "x"\n)]\nmod ffi_export {\n}\n'
cfg_last = '#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = "x"\n)]\n#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c")]\nmod ffi_export {\n}\n'
assert gateways(cfg_first) == [None]                    # the defect
assert gateways(cfg_last) == ['DEPS_LLHTTP_HTTP_C']
```

## Validation

None yet: the reproducer above shows the defect; the change's test is its two cases.

## Review

None yet.
PROPOSAL.md

# build.rs reads a gateway as switched when a multi-line attribute follows its `cfg`

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A defect, worked around. `build.rs`'s `gateway_lines` finds each `mod ffi_export` of `src/`
and the export feature gating it, which `gateways` and `export_dynamic_symbols` read: a
gateway with no feature is a switched module's, which the `system` feature refuses to link
an install beside, and whose `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` items every binary exports dynamically;
a gated one counts only when its feature is on. It takes the feature from a `#[cfg(feature =
"ffi-export-…")]` line and keeps it across the attribute lines after it, but resets it on
any line that neither starts with `#[` nor `//`. The second line of a multi-line attribute,
such as the region's own `#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = …\n)]`, the toolchain's
form for a region that takes the lint back, is such a line, so a gateway written as the
conventions have it, its `cfg` first, is read as having no feature: as a switched module's,
whether or not the feature is on.

## Evidence

- The reproducer below, from `wave-197/batch-0/run-1`, transcribes `gateway_lines` line for
  line. On a gateway written `cfg`
  then a multi-line `expect`, it reads no feature (`[None]`); with the `cfg` right above the
  `mod`, it reads `DEPS_LLHTTP_HTTP_C`. On `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs` at `b3d6b9b37`
  (`wave-194/batch-4/run-1`, before api.c's switch), whose gateway was gated so, it reads
  `[None]`: from that batch to the switch, a `system` build would have refused, naming
  `api.rs` as switched, and every build in shared mode would have passed
  `-Wl,--export-dynamic-symbol=` for api.c's 31 exports with the feature off, whose names
  the C defined.
- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`) wrote its gateway with the `cfg` right
  above `mod ffi_export`, after the `expect`, with a comment saying why.

## Destination

The campaign's `build.rs` (`gateway_lines`), which the `bindgen` skill's Build modes
section specifies: a gateway's feature is the `cfg` among the attributes of its `mod`,
wherever it stands among them.

## Change

Not made: `build.rs` is the bindings', and not a translator's to change. In
`gateway_lines`, track an attribute until its brackets close, so that the lines inside a
multi-line attribute neither set nor reset the gate:

```rust
// in the loop, before the `cfg` match:
if attr_depth > 0 {
    attr_depth += braces_of(t, '[', ']');
    continue;
}
if t.starts_with("#[") && braces_of(t, '[', ']') > 0 {
    attr_depth = braces_of(t, '[', ']');
    continue;
}
```

with `braces_of` counting the opening less the closing brackets, as `braces` counts braces.
A regression test of `gateway_lines` over both orders, the reproducer's two cases, keeps it.

## Reproducer

```python
"""build.rs's gateway_lines, line for line: the feature it reads for each `mod ffi_export`."""
def gateways(text):
    gate = None; out = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        t = line.strip()
        if t.startswith('#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-') and t.endswith('")]'):
            gate = t[len('#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-'):-3].upper().replace('-', '_')
        elif t.startswith('mod ffi_export') or t.startswith('pub mod ffi_export'):
            out.append(gate); gate = None
        elif not t.startswith('#[') and not t.startswith('//') and t:
            gate = None
    return out
cfg_first = '#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c")]\n#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = "x"\n)]\nmod ffi_export {\n}\n'
cfg_last = '#[expect(\n    unsafe_code,\n    reason = "x"\n)]\n#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c")]\nmod ffi_export {\n}\n'
assert gateways(cfg_first) == [None]                    # the defect
assert gateways(cfg_last) == ['DEPS_LLHTTP_HTTP_C']
```

None yet: the reproducer above shows the defect; the change's test is its two cases.

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  tsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    # glibc's tzset locks what TSan cannot see: see tsan.supp.
    export TSAN_OPTIONS=${TSAN_OPTIONS:-halt_on_error=1:suppressions=$here/crustify/scripts/tsan.supp}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" -Zbuild-std --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  bsan)
    # trybuild's nested cargo build does not finish under BorrowSanitizer, and the
    # compile-fail suite is a compile-time check the plain variant already runs.

# ffibox Generic smart pointers and traits for building safe Rust wrappers over C types and pointers, in both directions: memory C owns, held from Rust, and memory Rust owns that C holds, calls or reads. Designed for arbitrary user-space C interop, including the case where you need direct field access and a C-ABI-compatible layout (porting C internals to Rust in place), not just opaque-handle wrapping. ## Why Wrapping a C API in Rust means re-homing C's ownership and lifecycle conventions into RAII. The recurring shapes: - A C-allocated object with a destructor (`free`), and maybe a copy (`dup`). - A constructor or allocator (`foo_alloc`, `malloc`, `calloc`) whose result must be released by its paired free. - A refcounted object shared by several holders (`up_ref` / `unref`), maybe with a C lock over the state they mutate. - Types with multiple or runtime-conditional destructors. - A by-value struct whose teardown disposes its fields but not the struct. - An owned length-aware buffer or NUL-terminated `char *` with a C destructor. - A type-erased `void *` that stays opaque end to end. Each shape gets one owner type, generic over a **policy** — a type you declare that names the C routines. `impl_cdrop!` and its siblings bind a C routine to a policy; a type alias names the pair: `pub type FooBox = CBox;`. ## Mental model in one paragraph No reference to C-owned memory is formed while anything may write or free it: objects are reached through handles, and only a run of bytes nothing writes while it is lent is a `&CStr` or `&[u8]`. Each C type gets a layout type `Foo` (`#[repr(transparent)]` over `ffi::foo`; `Foo<'r>` when the C object borrows its parent) and two borrowed handles, `FooRef<'a>` / `FooMut<'a>`, each one pointer wide and carrying the getters and setters; field access projects a raw pointer out of the handle. Ownership comes in three shapes: `CBox` is the sole owner of an object behind a pointer and releases it through the policy `P`; `CArc` is one of several counted references and hands out the shared handle, the exclusive one only when the count proves it sole, and — for an object with a C lock — a `CGuard` whose `FooLocked<'a>` handle reaches the state that lock protects; and `CVal` holds the object inline and disposes its resources on drop. A policy that also constructs gives `CBox` and `CArc` safe constructors that allocate through it, so a safely built owner is always freed by the routine paired with its allocator. Strings, buffers and borrowed runs get their own types; a buffer drops its elements, so a `foo **` of owned objects releases each one. The other direction uses the same terms. `RustAlloc` is the policy over Rust's allocator, so an object Rust allocates is held as one C allocated, and `CAllocator` is a C allocation family as the standard `Allocator`, so a `Box` or `Vec` holds memory C frees; `CClosure` and `CPayload` put a Rust closure behind a C function pointer and its context, for one call or until C releases it; `CFn` and `CFnBox` hold a C function and its context that Rust calls, and `CCallback` and `CCallbackBox` either half; `CTable` holds Rust state behind a C table of function pointers C calls into, its slots minted by `impl_cvtable!` from a trait the Rust side implements; the `export_*!` macros offer a policy to C as the routine it calls, with the owner and handle types in its signature. [docs/ownership.md](docs/ownership.md) lists the owners and the policies; [docs/borrows.md](docs/borrows.md) lists the handles. Each walks from a C declaration to the type it wants. ## Install ```toml [dependencies] ffibox = "0.1" ``` ffibox needs Rust 1.100 or later (`rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`), the first release with the standard `Allocator` interface, which `CAllocator` implements over a C allocation family. ffibox is `#![no_std]`. The recurring shapes: - A C-allocated object with a destructor (`free`), and maybe a copy (`dup`). - A constructor or allocator (`foo_alloc`, `malloc`, `calloc`) whose result must be released by its paired free. - A refcounted object shared by several holders (`up_ref` / `unref`), maybe with a C lock over the state they mutate. - Types with multiple or runtime-conditional destructors. - A by-value struct whose teardown disposes its fields but not the struct. - An owned length-aware buffer or NUL-terminated `char *` with a C destructor. - A type-erased `void *` that stays opaque end to end. ## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them

## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them
- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded
- `cost` / `review cost` / `total` — a module's translation, review and combined cost;
  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant
  out, `Σ campaign` adds it, without per-unit cells
- `UB safe tests` … `Unit tests` — `#[test]` functions per suite, each with the coverage of
  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and
  those with a `Replaces:` or a `Wraps:` anchor at the tip; `share` is of the total

cat > crustify/tmp/linkcheck.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# The export-feature link check of wave-197/batch-1: the workspace's tests with
# ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c on, against private builds whose archive copy lacks
# deps/llhttp/http.c.o (the 168th member; transports/http.c.o, the 154th, stays), over a
# scratch tree with tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs retired as the switch retires it; then
# the variants' git2 and libgit2_tests relinked without deps/llhttp's http.c.o and with the
# crate's static library built with the feature on, and http-gate.sh over them, beside the
# stock variant's own run for tsan.
#   linkcheck.sh <variant>...
set -uo pipefail
W=/target/libgit2-crustify/crustify/.worktrees/modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/http.c/wave-197/batch-1
T=$W/crustify/tmp/linktree
S=$W/crustify/tmp/httpgate
G=$(realpath $W/crustify/builds)
F=ffi-export-deps-llhttp-http-c
export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=${CARGO_BUILD_JOBS:-24} RUST_TEST_THREADS=${RUST_TEST_THREADS:-24}
st=$W/crustify/tmp/linkcheck.status
# The scratch tree: the working tree's tracked files, the module's equivalence file retired.
if [ ! -d $T ]; then
  mkdir -p $T
  (cd $W && git ls-files -z --recurse-submodules=no | grep -zv '^c$' | xargs -0 cp --parents -t $T 2>/dev/null)
  ln -s $W/c $T/c
  rm -f $T/crustify/builds; ln -s $G $T/crustify/builds
  rm $T/tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/http.rs
  sed -i '/^mod http;$/d' $T/tests/equiv/deps/llhttp.rs
  (cd $T && git init -q && git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 && git -c user.name=x -c user.email=x@x commit -qm scratch)
fi
mkdir -p $S/gen; ln -sfn $G/c $S/gen/c
for v in "$@"; do
  V=$G/$v
  L=$W/crustify/tmp/linkcheck/$v
  if [ ! -d $L ]; then
    mkdir -p $L/crustify
    for e in $V/*; do n=$(basename $e); [ $n = crustify ] || ln -s $e $L/$n; done
    for e in $V/crustify/*; do n=$(basename $e); [ $n = libcrustify.a ] || ln -s $e $L/crustify/$n; done
    cp $V/crustify/libcrustify.a $L/crustify/ && ar dN 2 $L/crustify/libcrustify.a http.c.o
  fi
  echo "$v archive: $(ar t $L/crustify/libcrustify.a | wc -l) members, $(nm -A $L/crustify/libcrustify.a 2>/dev/null | grep -cE ' T (llhttp_should_keep_alive|llhttp__after_headers_complete)$') http.c symbols, transport $(nm -A $L/crustify/libcrustify.a 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' T git_smart_subtransport_http$')" >> $st
  (cd $T && CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$L CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$W/crustify/tmp/lc-target/$v crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh $v clippy --workspace --all-targets --features $F -- -D warnings) > $W/crustify/tmp/lc-clippy-$v.log 2>&1; echo "$v clippy-feature $?" >> $st
  (cd $T && CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$L CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$W/crustify/tmp/lc-target/$v crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh $v test --workspace --no-fail-fast --features $F) > $W/crustify/tmp/lc-test-$v.log 2>&1; echo "$v test-feature $?" >> $st
  # The Rust static library, as rust-staticlib.sh builds it, with the export feature on.
  (cd $T && CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$L CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$S/cargo-$v \
    crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh $v rustc -p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked \
    --features bindgen,$F --crate-type staticlib) >$S/staticlib-$v.log 2>&1 || { echo "$v staticlib failed" >> $st; continue; }
  lib=$(ls $S/cargo-$v/debug/liblibgit2_crustify.a $S/cargo-$v/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug/liblibgit2_crustify.a 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  mkdir -p $S/gen/$v
  for t in git2 libgit2_tests; do
    cmd=$(ninja -C $V -t commands $t | tail -1)
    case "$cmd" in *" deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o "*) ;; *) echo "$v $t: no http.c.o input" >> $st; continue 2;; esac
    cmd=${cmd//" deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o "/" "}
    cmd=${cmd//" crustify/liblibgit2_crustify.a"/" $lib"}
    cmd=${cmd//" -o $t "/" -o $S/gen/$v/$t "}
    (cd $V && eval "$cmd") >$S/link-$v-$t.log 2>&1 || { echo "$v $t link failed" >> $st; continue 2; }
  done
  echo "$v relinked git2 exports: $(nm $S/gen/$v/git2 | grep -cE ' T (llhttp_should_keep_alive|llhttp__before_headers_complete|llhttp__after_headers_complete|llhttp__after_message_complete)$'), needs_eof: $(nm $S/gen/$v/git2 | grep -c ' llhttp_message_needs_eof$')" >> $st
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=/dev/null $W/crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh $S/gen/$v $S/out-$v >$S/http-gate-$v.log 2>&1
  echo "$v http-gate $?" >> $st
  if [ $v = tsan ]; then
    ln -sfn $G/tsan $S/stock-tsan 2>/dev/null
    LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=/dev/null $W/crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh $G/tsan $S/out-stock-tsan >$S/http-gate-stock-tsan.log 2>&1
    echo "stock tsan http-gate $?" >> $st
  fi
done
echo done >> $st
EOF
chmod +x crustify/tmp/linkcheck.sh; rm -f crustify/tmp/linkcheck.status; nohup crustify/tmp/linkcheck.sh plain asan-ubsan tsan > crustify/tmp/linkcheck.out 2>&1 &
echo $! > crustify/tmp/linkcheck.pid; cat crustify/tmp/linkcheck.pid

content.content:
# Counter schema

The counters ffimap reports: what each one holds, how a record is shaped, and
how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
and no dataflow is performed.

What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is

  their lifecycle through an ffibox contract, which none of the std shares can
  see.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.pub_field.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that publish
  the pointer as a public field. Not a declaration: an access the type does not
  govern.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: the type
  stores a pointer and declares nothing about it, in any vocabulary.
- `ty.wrapping_unsafe_cell.{pub,priv}` -- types holding an `UnsafeCell`, the
  one way to hold a value C may write while Rust holds a shared reference to it.
- `ty.impl_block.{pub,priv}` -- inherent `impl T` blocks: the API the crate
  wrote for its own type.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.ffibox.{layout,ref,mut,locked}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the blocks on a cell and on each of its handles, which are different
  surfaces: the layout type carries the constructors, the shared handle the
  getters, the exclusive handle the setters.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the blocks on everything else.
- `ty.impl_trait.{pub,priv}` -- `impl Tr for T` blocks: satisfying someone
  else's shape.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.unsafe` -- of those, the `unsafe impl`s, which assert
  what the compiler cannot check. `TrivialClone`, which `#[derive(Clone)]`
  emits, is skipped.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a `#[derive]` wrote.
  Nobody typed them, and they are most of the `std` arm.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.drop.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a
  standard-library trait, by trait: `Drop`, which runs code when an object is
  released.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.clone.{pub,priv}` -- `Clone`, which duplicates
  one.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` -- `Send`, the claim that an
  object may move to another thread.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}` -- `Sync`, the claim that it may
  be shared between threads.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.ref_forming.{pub,priv}` -- `Deref`, `DerefMut`,
  `AsRef`, `AsMut`, `Borrow`, `BorrowMut`, `Index` and `IndexMut`, whose
  method returns a reference of a type the impl chose.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.other.{pub,priv}` -- every other std trait:
  `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Copy` and the rest.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.local.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a trait the crate
  declared itself: a shape it chose rather than adopted.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of an ffibox
  trait that states a cell's layout or how it is reached and locked: the
  layout, seam and guard groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, likewise.
- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of

  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, likewise.
- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of
  parameter. A lifetime ties the type to something it borrows; a type parameter
  makes it a family rather than one layout, so each instantiation is a separate
  question about C's bytes. A type may carry both.
- `ty.generic.of_which.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- the generic types that
  hold a raw pointer.
- `ty.field.ffibox.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- fields holding an ffibox
  primitive, by primitive: the delegation `ty.storing_raw_ptr` deliberately
  does not count as the crate's own pointer.

model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|

| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |

| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |

usage: ffimap [-h] [--sites COUNTER [COUNTER ...]]
              [--sys-crates CRATE[,CRATE...]] [--seams NAMES]
              [--regions NAMES] [--barriers NAMES]
              [--features FEATURE[,FEATURE...]] [--ffibox]
              WORKSPACE

Scan a Rust crate's unsafe surface and raw-pointer usage with a rustc driver
over HIR and typeck. Reproducible: same tree, same bytes. Needs the crate to
compile; when it does not, there are no counts rather than approximate ones.
It says HOW MUCH unsafety is there, never which of it is wrong.

positional arguments:
  WORKSPACE             Directory of the Cargo workspace (or package) to scan.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --sites COUNTER [COUNTER ...]
                        Also report where these counters' increments are in
                        the source: a `sites` record beside `counts` with one
                        list per counter. Takes a counter's dotted path down
                        to its LEAF (e.g. raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub,
                        ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub,
                        code.unsafe_call.ffi): a path that stops at an arm
                        above one validates and then reads empty, since the
                        driver emits by leaf. Line totals have no sites.
  --sys-crates CRATE[,CRATE...]
                        Crates whose #[repr(C)] types are C's: the crate's own
                        bindings and any other crate it reaches C through,
                        such as `libc`. The field walk descends through them
                        too, so a pointer a scanned type holds through one is
                        counted as the scanned crate's to manage. Nothing is
                        discovered: a Cargo `links` key and a `*-sys` name
                        both over-report, so unnamed means the peel set is the
                        scanned crate alone.
  --seams NAMES         Function names that are seams -- the conversion
                        between a wrapper and its raw pointer (`raw`,
                        `from_raw`, `as_ptr`, `from_ptr`). Newline- or comma-
                        separated, so `--seams "$(cat seams.txt)"` works. They
                        are counted as usual and ALSO reported as the
                        `of_which.seam` share of each fn-signature counter, so
                        a reader can tell plumbing from the pointer management
                        a consumer of the safe API actually faces. ffimap
                        never guesses the names.
  --regions NAMES       Module names that are regions -- the modules a crate
                        confines a kind of code to, such as its unsafe FFI
                        (`ffi_import`, `ffi_export`). Newline- or comma-
                        separated. The unsafe blocks are then reported by the
                        region they sit in, as
                        code.unsafe_block.of_which.region.<name>, with the
                        rest as outside_regions, and the unsafe fns outside

content.content:
# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
1:# API stability per C item

40:## 2. C items and their stand-ins
60:## 3. Locators and paths
90:## 4. Signatures
123:## 5. Handles and owners
148:## 6. The contract view
225:## 7. The unattributed surface
232:## 8. Coverage
241:## 9. The extract
272:## 10. The diff
332:## 11. What the measure cannot see

content.content:
baseline.sh
mark.py
report.py
run.sh
#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"

# llhttp.c's equivalence tests call api.c functions that have no export, unlinking `equiv` at the switch

- **finding**: `misc/llhttp-equiv-tests-call-api-c-functions-without-exports`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s module pass
- **items**: the 13 api.c functions ported onto `llhttp.rs`'s accessors and maps and left
  unexported, since no C outside api.c calls them: `fn::llhttp_get_type`,
  `fn::llhttp_get_http_major`, `fn::llhttp_get_http_minor`, `fn::llhttp_get_method`,
  `fn::llhttp_get_status_code`, `fn::llhttp_get_upgrade`, `fn::llhttp_get_errno`,
  `fn::llhttp_errno_name`, `fn::llhttp_method_name`, `fn::llhttp_status_name`, with
  `fn::llhttp_settings_init`; and the tests of `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`
  (`wave-194/batch-0`, `1ead111ee`, and `wave-194/batch-1`, `2c69341c3`) that call them
- **affected commit**: `9124cc5a6`
- **files**: `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`, `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

At api.c's switch, `api.c.o` leaves the variants' archives, and the 31 exports of
`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` are all that define api.c's symbols. The batches before this
one checked that with archive copies lacking `api.c.o`, and left `equiv` out "by design": its
api.c comparisons call api.c's C and retire with it. But `equiv` is one binary, for every
module of the crate, and not only `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` calls api.c.
`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`, the equivalence tests of `llhttp.c`, which stays C, reads
both its parsers through api.c's getters (`c_fields`), checks the setters through
`llhttp_get_type` and `llhttp_get_upgrade`, compares the maps with api.c's three name
functions, and builds a table with `llhttp_settings_init`. None of those has an export. So once
only `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` is retired, `equiv` does not link, and with it neither
`llhttp.c`'s surviving equivalence tests (`llhttp__internal_init` and
`llhttp__internal_execute`, which stay) nor any other module's run.

## Evidence

On `9124cc5a6`, with `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain` a copy of the `plain` variant's build
whose archive lacks `api.c.o` (each entry of `crustify/builds/plain` symlinked but
`crustify/libcrustify.a`, copied and then `ar d crustify/libcrustify.a api.c.o`, 211
objects), from the repository root:

```
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$PWD/crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target/linkcheck-plain \
crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh plain test --features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c --test equiv --no-run
```

`rust-lld` stops at its limit of 20 undefined symbols (`link-affected.log`); 10 of the
references it lists are `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`'s:

```text
rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: llhttp_get_type
          >>> referenced by llhttp.rs:78 (tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs:78)
          >>> referenced by llhttp.rs:324 (tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs:324)
rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: llhttp_settings_init
          >>> referenced by api.rs:202 (tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs:202)
          >>> referenced by llhttp.rs:250 (tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs:250)
…
rust-lld: error: too many errors emitted, stopping now (use --error-limit=0 to see all errors)
```

The three name functions, which the limit hides, are the other three of the file's 23
unexported symbols. Every other suite already links against the exports (batch 6's check).

## Fix

In this batch's second commit, the nine tests that compare `llhttp.rs`'s accessors and maps
with api.c's getters and name functions move, unchanged, from
`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs` to an inline module `getters` of
`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`: they test api.c's ported items, whose anchors are
`Replaces fn::llhttp_get_*`, so they are api.c's and retire with its C. The file
`llhttp.rs` keeps the tests that compare `llhttp.c`'s Rust with `llhttp.c`'s C, and calls no
api.c function. Retiring `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` alone, and its `mod api;`, is then
api.c's whole equivalence retirement. In a scratch tree with that file retired, the workspace
links against the exports and passes on `plain` (`equiv` 532), and on ASan+UBSan and TSan but
for the known nightly failures.

## What the retiring tests established, and which unit test keeps it

Retiring `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` removes 21 `equiv` tests. `unit_pub` keeps, in
`tests/unit_pub/deps/llhttp/api.rs` unless named otherwise:

| retiring `equiv` test | kept by |
|---|---|
| `new_leaves_the_table_as_llhttp_settings_init_does` | `new_and_default_are_empty_tables`, `a_zeroed_table_is_empty` |
| `the_setters_fill_the_table_as_c_fills_its_fields` | `each_setter_sets_its_own_slot_and_none_clears_it`, `a_setter_replaces_what_its_slot_held_and_leaves_the_others`, `a_slot_read_back_calls_the_handler_it_was_set_to` |
======

content.content:
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

PER_BINARY = {"miri", "bsan"}


class Refused(Exception):
    """The run cannot start: a bad argument, tree or skip."""


def git(tree: Path, *args: str) -> str:
        skips.setdefault(stage, {}).setdefault(binary, []).append(name)
    return skips


class Gates:
    def __init__(self, a: argparse.Namespace, snap: Path, logs: Path):
        self.a, self.snap, self.logs = a, snap, logs
        self.runner = shlex.split(a.runner)
        self.results: list[dict] = []
        self.stage_env: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        for spec in a.stage_env:
            stage, _, kv = spec.partition(":")
            k, eq, v = kv.partition("=")
            if not (stage and k and eq):
                raise Refused(f"--stage-env {spec}: expected <stage>:<K>=<V>")
            self.stage_env.setdefault(stage, {})[k] = v

    def env(self, stage: str, **extra: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        env = dict(os.environ)
        if stage == "miri":
            # Miri's builds kept apart from the variants', in the snapshot's target dir.
            env.setdefault("CARGO_TARGET_DIR", str(self.snap / "target" / "miri"))
        env.update(self.stage_env.get(stage, {}))
        env.update(extra)
        return env

    def cargo(self, stage: str) -> list[str]:
        """The command that runs cargo for `stage`, up to its subcommand."""
        if stage == "miri":
            return ["cargo", f"+{self.a.nightly}", "miri"]
        return [*self.runner, stage]

    def run(self, stage: str, name: str, cmd: list[str], env: dict[str, str],
            timeout: int | None = None) -> dict:
        log = self.logs / f"{name}.log"
        start = time.monotonic()
        timed_out = False
        with open(log, "w") as out:
            out.write(f"$ {shlex.join(cmd)}\n")
            out.flush()
            proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=self.snap, env=env, stdout=out,
                                    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
            try:
                rc = proc.wait(timeout=timeout)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                timed_out = True
                os.killpg(proc.pid, 9)
                rc = proc.wait()
        text = log.read_text(errors="replace")
        result = {
            "stage": stage, "run": name, "command": shlex.join(cmd), "exit": rc,
            "timed_out": timed_out, "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - start, 1),
            "results": [l for l in text.splitlines() if l.startswith("test result:")],
            "failed": sorted({l[5:-len(" ... FAILED")] for l in text.splitlines()
                              if l.startswith("test ") and l.endswith(" ... FAILED")}),
            "log": str(log),
        }
        self.results.append(result)
        self.write_summary()
        return result

    def write_summary(self) -> None:
        (self.logs / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(self.results, indent=1) + "\n")
        lines = []
        for r in self.results:
            state = "timed out" if r["timed_out"] else f"exit {r['exit']}"
            lines.append(f"{r['run']}: {state}, {r['seconds']} s")
            lines += [f"  {l}" for l in r["results"]]
            lines += [f"  FAILED {t}" for t in r["failed"]]
        (self.logs / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

    def listed(self, stage: str, package: str, binary: str) -> set[str]:
        cmd = [*self.cargo(stage), "test", "-p", package, *selector(binary), "--",
               "--list", "--format", "terse"]
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=self.snap, env=self.env(stage), capture_output=True,
                             text=True)
        if out.returncode != 0:
            raise Refused(f"{shlex.join(cmd)} failed:\n{out.stderr[-4000:]}")
        return {l.rsplit(": ", 1)[0] for l in out.stdout.splitlines()
                if l.endswith(": test") or l.endswith(": bench")}

    def check_skips(self, skips, package: str, bins: list[str]) -> None:
        stages = self.a.stages
        for stage in skips:
            if stage not in stages:
                continue
            for binary, names in skips[stage].items():
                if binary not in bins:
                    raise Refused(f"skip of {stage}: {package} has no test binary {binary}")
                listed = self.listed("plain" if stage not in PER_BINARY else stage,
                                     package, binary)
                missing = [n for n in names if n not in listed]
                if missing:
                    raise Refused(f"skips of {stage} name no test of {binary}: "
                                  + ", ".join(missing))
                # libtest skips by substring unless `--exact`, which would also make
                # exact any substring skip the runner adds, such as `compile_fail`:
                # a skip is taken only where it names its test alone.
                wider = {n: sorted(t for t in listed if n in t and t != n) for n in names}
                wider = {n: ts for n, ts in wider.items() if ts}
                if wider:
                    raise Refused(f"skips of {stage} in {binary} would also skip: "
                                  + "; ".join(f"{n} -> {', '.join(ts)}"
                                              for n, ts in wider.items()))

    @staticmethod
    def skip_args(names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        return [a for n in names for a in ("--skip", n)]

    def variant(self, stage: str, skips) -> None:
        names = sorted({n for ns in skips.get(stage, {}).values() for n in ns})
        cmd = [*self.cargo(stage), "test", "--workspace", "--no-fail-fast"]
        extra = self.skip_args(names)
        self.run(stage, stage, cmd + (["--", *extra] if extra else []), self.env(stage))

    def per_binary(self, stage: str, package: str, bins: list[str], skips) -> None:
        env = self.env(stage)
        build = self.run(stage, f"{stage}-build",
                         [*self.cargo(stage), "test", "-p", package, "--no-run"], env)
        if build["exit"] != 0:
            return
        timeout = self.a.timeout if stage == "bsan" else None

        def one(binary: str) -> None:
            names = list(skips.get(stage, {}).get(binary, []))
            tail = self.skip_args(names)
            if stage == "miri":
                tail += ["--skip", "compile_fail"]
            cmd = [*self.cargo(stage), "test", "-p", package, *selector(binary)]
            self.run(stage, f"{stage}-{binary}", cmd + (["--", *tail] if tail else []), env,
                     timeout)

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.a.parallel or len(bins)) as pool:
            list(pool.map(one, bins))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="end-gates", description=__doc__,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("tree", type=Path, nargs="?")
    p.add_argument("--logs", type=Path, help="the dir each run's log and the summary go to")
    p.add_argument("--stages", default="plain,asan-ubsan,tsan,miri,bsan",
                   help="comma-separated, run in this order (default: %(default)s)")
    src = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    src.add_argument("--rev", default="HEAD", help="the commit to snapshot (default: HEAD)")
    src.add_argument("--working-tree", action="store_true",
                     help="snapshot the working tree, tracked and untracked files git keeps")
    p.add_argument("--label", help="the snapshot's name under crustify/tmp (default: the rev)")
    p.add_argument("--package", help="the package whose test binaries run per binary "
                                     "(default: the workspace's root package)")
    p.add_argument("--runner", default="crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh",
                   help="the command that runs cargo against a variant, given the variant "
                        "first (default: %(default)s, from the snapshot)")
    p.add_argument("--link", action="append", default=[],
                   help="a path git leaves out, symlinked from the tree (repeatable); "
                        "submodules are linked always")
    p.add_argument("--skip-file", type=Path, help="lines of `<stage> <binary> <test name>`")
    p.add_argument("--stage-env", action="append", default=[],
                   help="<stage>:<K>=<V>, set for that stage's runs (repeatable)")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=3600,
                   help="seconds each BSan binary may run (default: %(default)s)")
    p.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=0,
                   help="test binaries run side by side (default: all)")
    p.add_argument("--nightly", help="Miri's toolchain (default: the workspace's "
                                     "`nightly` key, else the rust-toolchain file's)")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    if a.tree is None or a.logs is None:
        p.error("the tree and --logs are required")
    try:
        tree = a.tree.resolve()
        a.stages = [s for s in a.stages.split(",") if s]
        rev = None if a.working_tree else a.rev
        label = a.label or ("working-tree" if rev is None
                            else git(tree, "rev-parse", "--short", rev).strip())
        snap = tree / "crustify" / "tmp" / f"gates-{label}"
        logs = a.logs.resolve()
        logs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        snapshot(tree, snap, rev, a.link)
        if a.nightly is None and "miri" in a.stages:
            a.nightly = nightly_of(snap)
        gates = Gates(a, snap, logs)
        skips = read_skips(a.skip_file)
        unknown = set(skips) - set(a.stages)
        if unknown:
            print(f"end-gates: skips of stages not run, ignored: {sorted(unknown)}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        package, bins = package_binaries(snap, a.package)
        gates.check_skips(skips, package, bins)
    except (Refused, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as e:
        print(f"end-gates: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(f"end-gates: snapshot {snap}, logs {logs}", file=sys.stderr)
    for stage in a.stages:

#[test]
fn slow() { std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60)); }
#[test]
fn sees_its_builds() {
    let here = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    assert!(here.join("builds/marker").exists());
}
"""

# A runner that takes the variant first, as a campaign's does, and runs plain cargo.
RUNNER = """#!/bin/sh
echo "variant $1" >&2
shift
exec cargo "$@"
"""


def sh(cwd: Path, *cmd: str) -> None:
    subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True)


@unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which("cargo") and shutil.which("git"), "needs cargo and git")
class EndGates(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        t = self.tree = self.tmp / "tree"
        (t / "src").mkdir(parents=True)
        (t / "tests").mkdir()
        (t / "Cargo.toml").write_text(
            '[package]\nname = "demo"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2021"\n\n'
            '[workspace]\n')
        (t / "src/lib.rs").write_text(LIB)
        (t / "tests/it.rs").write_text(IT)
        (t / ".gitignore").write_text("/target\n/builds\n/crustify/tmp\n")
        (t / "builds").mkdir()
        (t / "builds/marker").write_text("")
        self.runner = self.tmp / "runner.sh"
        self.runner.write_text(RUNNER)
        self.runner.chmod(0o755)
        sh(t, "git", "init", "-q")
        sh(t, "git", "add", "-A")
        sh(t, "git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "commit", "-qm", "init")
        self.logs = self.tmp / "logs"
        os.environ.setdefault("CARGO_HOME", "/root/.cargo")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def gates(self, *args: str, skips: str | None = None) -> int:
        argv = [str(self.tree), "--logs", str(self.logs), "--runner", str(self.runner),
                "--link", "builds", *args]
        if skips is not None:
            f = self.tmp / "skips"
            f.write_text(skips)
            argv += ["--skip-file", str(f)]
        return eg.main(argv)

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
        return {r["run"]: r for r in
                json.loads((self.logs / "summary.json").read_text())}

    def test_snapshot_is_the_commit_with_links_and_a_repository(self) -> None:
        (self.tree / "src/lib.rs").write_text("uncommitted")
        (self.tree / "untracked.txt").write_text("")
        snap = self.tmp / "snap"
        eg.snapshot(self.tree, snap, "HEAD", ["builds"])
        self.assertEqual((snap / "src/lib.rs").read_text(), LIB)
        self.assertFalse((snap / "untracked.txt").exists())
        self.assertTrue((snap / "builds").is_symlink())
        self.assertTrue((snap / "builds/marker").exists())
        self.assertTrue((snap / ".git").is_dir())

    def test_working_tree_snapshot_takes_uncommitted_and_untracked_files(self) -> None:
        (self.tree / "src/lib.rs").write_text("uncommitted")
        (self.tree / "untracked.txt").write_text("")
        snap = self.tmp / "snap"
        eg.snapshot(self.tree, snap, None, [])
        self.assertEqual((snap / "src/lib.rs").read_text(), "uncommitted")
        self.assertTrue((snap / "untracked.txt").exists())
        self.assertFalse((snap / "target").exists())

    def test_a_tracked_path_is_not_linked(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(eg.Refused):
            eg.snapshot(self.tree, self.tmp / "snap", "HEAD", ["src"])

    def test_a_skip_that_names_no_test_fails_before_any_stage(self) -> None:
        rc = self.gates("--stages", "plain", skips="plain lib tests::none\n")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 2)
        self.assertFalse((self.logs / "plain.log").exists())

    def test_a_skip_that_would_skip_another_test_fails(self) -> None:
        rc = self.gates("--stages", "plain", skips="plain lib tests::one\n")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 2)
        self.assertFalse((self.logs / "plain.log").exists())

    def test_a_skip_of_an_unknown_binary_fails(self) -> None:
        rc = self.gates("--stages", "plain", skips="plain nope tests::one_more\n")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 2)

    def test_stages_run_in_order_with_their_skips_and_env(self) -> None:
        rc = self.gates("--stages", "plain,bsan", "--stage-env", "plain:DEMO_FAIL=1",
                        skips="# hangs\nplain it slow\nbsan it slow\n")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
        s = self.summary()
        self.assertEqual(list(s)[:2], ["plain", "bsan-build"])
        self.assertEqual(set(list(s)[2:]), {"bsan-lib", "bsan-it"})
        self.assertNotEqual(s["plain"]["exit"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(s["plain"]["failed"], ["tests::fails_on_demand"])
        self.assertIn("--skip slow", s["plain"]["command"])
        for run in ("bsan-build", "bsan-lib", "bsan-it"):
            self.assertEqual(s[run]["exit"], 0, run)
        self.assertIn("--skip slow", s["bsan-it"]["command"])
        self.assertNotIn("--skip", s["bsan-lib"]["command"])
        self.assertIn("variant bsan", Path(s["bsan-it"]["log"]).read_text())
        self.assertTrue(any("3 passed" in l or "2 passed" in l
                            for l in s["bsan-it"]["results"]))
        self.assertIn("plain: exit", (self.logs / "summary.txt").read_text())

    def test_a_binary_past_its_timeout_is_reported_and_fails(self) -> None:
        rc = self.gates("--stages", "bsan", "--timeout", "20")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
        s = self.summary()
        self.assertTrue(s["bsan-it"]["timed_out"])
        self.assertFalse(s["bsan-lib"]["timed_out"])
        self.assertEqual(s["bsan-lib"]["exit"], 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
